p0.en: Key issue: How the brain produces behavioral and psychological processes

p2.original: 脑由许多专门化的模块构成，它们一起工作创造出了心理和行为。
p2.en: The brain consists of many specialized modules that work together to create psychology and behaviour.

p3.original: 1848年9月，一名25岁的美国铁路工人菲尼亚斯·盖奇（Phineas Gage）的头部受了很严重的伤。当时炸药爆炸使得一根铁棒从他的面部插入，穿过他的脑前部，最后从他的头顶穿出（见下图）。
p3.en: In September 1848, a 25-year-old United States railway worker, Phineas Gage, sustained severe head injuries. The explosion caused an iron bar to be inserted from his face, through the front of his head and finally from the top of his head (see figure below).

p4.original: 本书作者菲利普·津巴多和菲尼亚斯·盖奇的头骨。
p4.en: The authors of this book are Philip Zimbabwe and the skull of Finyas Gage.

p5.original: 令人惊讶的是，盖奇竟然从这次重伤中恢复了，并且又活了12年，但他却变成了一个心理上不同的人（Fleischman，2002；Macmillan，2000）。认识他的人都说，盖奇曾经是一个可靠的、讨人喜欢的工头，但是后来他成了一个不负责任的、粗鲁的痞子。他从前的同事说：“这个盖奇不再是那个盖奇了。”（Damasio，1994）我们不禁想知道：他受伤的位置，也就是脑前部，是否是曾经的那个“盖奇”的家？盖奇转变的故事听起来和吉尔·波特·泰勒的经历非常相似，她说，自她中风之后，她变成了“另一个人”。我们怎么解释这些变化？
p5.en: Surprisingly, Gekchi recovered from this serious injury and lived for 12 years, but he became a different person (Fleischman, 2002); Macmillan, 2000. Those who knew him said that Gage had been a reliable, attractive foreman, but that he had since become an irresponsible, rude bastard. His former colleague said, "This Gage is not the Gage anymore. (Damasio, 1994) We wonder: Is he injured in the front of his head, or is he the home of the once-Gecchi? The story of Gage's transition sounds very similar to what Gil Potter Taylor had experienced, and she said that she had become “another person” since her stroke. How do we explain these changes?

p6.original: 这些故事也引出了一个更大的问题：心理和身体之间的联系是什么？当然，长久以来人类就知道两者之间是有联系的，虽然他们并不确定脑是心理的器官。即使到今天，我们还会像莎士比亚的时代一样，用“把我的心给你”来形容爱上某个人，或者说某样东西“令人反胃”来表达厌恶。不过我们都已经知道爱并不是来自于心脏，厌恶也不是来自于消化系统，相反，所有的情绪、欲望和思想都源于脑。（显然，作曲家还不知道这个事实，他们写抒情歌曲的时候可不会写“我用我全部的脑来爱你”。）
p6.en: These stories also raise a bigger question: what is the connection between the mind and the body? Of course, for a long time humans knew that there was a link between the two, although they were not sure that the brain was a mental organ. Even today, we're going to use the words “put my heart to you” to describe falling in love with someone, or something that's disgusting” as Shakespeare's era. But we all know that love does not come from the heart, nor from the digestive system, but rather from the brain. (It is clear that composers are not aware of this fact, and they don't write "I love you with all my brains" when they write love songs. I don't think so.

p7.original: 最终，神经科学家揭开了这个复杂的心理器官的深层秘密。我们现在知道脑是一组不同模块的组合，它们像计算机的组块一样协同工作。对脑的这种看法构成了本节的核心概念。
p7.en: Ultimately, neuroscientists reveal the deep secrets of this complex mental organ. Now we know that the brain is a combination of different modules that work together like a computer's block. This perception of the brain forms the core concept of this section.

p8.original: 脑由许多专门化的模块构成，它们一起工作创造出了心理和行为。
p8.en: The brain consists of many specialized modules that work together to create psychology and behaviour.

p9.original: 当你研究脑时，你会发现脑的每一个模块都有自己的职责功能（Cohen & Tong，2001）。某些模块负责加工感觉，例如，视觉和听觉；某些模块负责调节我们的情绪；某些模块负责记忆；还有一些模块负责生成语言和其他行为。其中的要点在于，脑的各个专门模块就像一支冠军团队的成员一样：每个人只负责一项特定的工作，但是全员配合良好。令人高兴的是，许多模块可以自动完成它们的任务，不需要意识的参与。例如，你可以在走路的同时，消化你的早餐，保持呼吸，还可以和他人交谈。但是，当脑的一个或多个模块出现问题（例如，中风或像菲尼亚斯·盖奇一样受伤）时，思想和行为的生物学基础就会浮出水面。
p9.en: When you study the brain, you find that each module of the brain has its own function (Cohen & Tong, 2001). Some modules are responsible for processing feelings, e.g. visual and hearing; Some modules are responsible for regulating our emotions; Some modules are for memory; There are also modules for generating language and other behaviours. The main point is that the specialized modules of the brain are like members of a champion team: each person is responsible for only one particular job, but the whole team works well. It is gratifying that many modules can automatically accomplish their tasks without the need for conscious participation. For example, you can walk while digesting your breakfast, breathing and talking to others. However, when one or more modules of the brain have problems (e.g. strokes or injuries like Finyas Gage) the biological basis of thought and behaviour emerges.

p10.original: 让我们追随神经科学家探索脑内部工作的脚步来开始讲述大脑的故事吧。
p10.en: Let's follow the steps of neuroscientists to explore inside their brains to start telling the story of the brain.

p19.original: 脑被颅骨保护着，与外界隔绝，它并没有真的触摸天鹅绒、品尝巧克力、发生性行为或看见蓝色的天空。它只能通过外周神经系统（充当脑和外部世界的连接）中的电化学活动变化模式来间接地了解外部世界。为了与身体的不同部位沟通，脑必须依赖神经和内分泌系统与遍布全身的肌肉、器官和腺体进行信息传递。
p19.en: The brain is protected by the skull, isolated from the outside world, and it does not really touch velvet, taste chocolate, have sex or see the blue sky. It can only indirectly understand the outside world by changing patterns of electrochemical activity in the outer nervous system (which acts as a link between the brain and the outside world). In order to communicate with different parts of the body, the brain must rely on the nervous and endocrine systems for the transmission of information with muscles, organs and glands throughout the body.

p20.original: 但是，如果你可以从颅骨之下窥视脑，你会看见什么？它遍布皱纹的表面使它看起来像一颗巨大的核桃，这并不能告诉我们脑的内部结构和功能。脑电图、电刺激和不同类型的脑部扫描技术为我们了解脑开启了新的窗口。
p20.en: But if you could look under the skull, what would you see? It's covered in wrinkles that make it look like a giant walnut, which does not tell us the internal structure and function of the brain. EEGs, electro-stimulations and different types of brain scanning technologies open new windows for our understanding of the brain.

p22.original: 大约100年前，神经科学家开始将电极贴在头皮上，使用脑电图（electro-encephalograph，EEG）来记录微弱的电压变化模式，这种电压变化被称为脑电波。就像城市的灯光可以提示夜晚哪里最热闹一样，EEG可以感知脑的哪个部分最活跃。例如，EEG可以确定哪些脑区参与了手的移动，哪些脑区加工了视觉图像。它也可以揭示由脑功能障碍引起的异常波，例如，癫痫（epilepsy，一种脑中的电“风暴”引起的痉挛性疾病）。你可以在下图中看到EEG所得到的数据信息。
p22.en: About 100 years ago, neuroscientists began to post electrodes on their heads, using electro-encephalic maps (electro-cenphalograp, EEG) to document weak voltage patterns, known as brain waves. Just as the lights in the city can tell where the hottest at night is, the EEG can sense which part of the brain is most active. For example, EEG can determine which brain regions are involved in hand movements and which brain areas are processed for visual images. It can also reveal an abnormal wave caused by brain dysfunction, e.g. epilepsy (epilipsy, a convulsive disease caused by electrical “storms” in the brain). You can see the data information that EEG has.

p23.original: EEG可记录脑电波活动。它可以被用来检查异常的脑电波模式，这些模式可以用于检测癫痫、中风或脑损伤、痴呆或睡眠障碍。
p23.en: EEG can record brain wave activity. It can be used to detect abnormal brain wave patterns, which can be used to detect epilepsy, stroke or brain damage, dementia or sleep disorders.

p24.original: 然而，EEG虽然很有用，但不是很精确，它只能粗略地记录电极附近大范围内的脑电波活动。由于使用的电极可能少于12个，EEG不能绘制出详细的脑电波地形图。相反，它只是对数百万个神经元产生的电波活动进行粗略的、瞬时的汇总。令人惊讶的是，我们有时竟然可以从EEG的数据中获取心理活动的痕迹。
p24.en: However, EEG, although useful, is not very precise and can only record roughly large areas of brain wave activity near the electrodes. EEG was unable to produce detailed EEG maps of the electro-temperature landscape, as the number of electrodes used may be less than 12. Instead, it provides a rough, instant summary of the electrical wave activity generated by millions of neurons. Surprisingly, we can sometimes extract traces of psychological activity from EEG data.

p25.original: 2.7.2 用电探针绘制脑地形图
p25.en: 2.7.2 Producing brain topography with electric probes

p26.original: 半个世纪之前，人们对脑的理解又往前迈了一步。伟大的加拿大神经学家怀尔德·彭菲尔德（Wilder Penfield）绘制了脑粉灰色表面的地形图，这为我们了解脑提供了一条新的途径。在脑手术期间，彭菲尔德使用一支笔形电探针，用微弱的电流刺激病人暴露出来的脑，然后记录病人的反应（他的病人也是保持清醒状态，不过由于局部麻醉的作用，他们并没有感到疼痛）。
p26.en: Half a century ago, people took another step forward in understanding the brain. The great Canadian neurologist Wilder Penfield has drawn a topographic map of the grey surface of the brain, which provides us with a new way of understanding the brain. During the brain surgery, Penfield used a pen-shaped electric probe to stimulate the patient's brain exposure with a weak current and then document the patient's reaction (his patients were also sober, although they did not feel pain due to the effects of local anesthesia).

p27.original: 这不只是一个满足好奇心的实验。作为一个外科医生，彭菲尔德需要确定脑病变区域的边界以避免切除健康的组织。在探测过程中，他发现大脑表面不同的区域有不同的功能——在几十年前，这是一个多么激动人心的发现！刺激某一个点可能会让人的左手动一下；另一个点可能会让人产生一个感觉，例如，闪光；刺激有些点偶尔还会让人回忆起童年的事情（Penfield，1959；Penfield & Baldwin，1952）。后来，另一些科学家紧随其后，开始探索脑的更深层次的结构。研究人员们发现，电刺激可以引发一系列复杂的行为或情绪。这一系列研究工作的结论是非常明确的：每一个脑区都有自己特定的功能。
p27.en: It's not just an experiment to satisfy curiosity. As a surgeon, Penfield needs to define the boundaries of the brain-disordered area to avoid the removal of healthy tissues. In the process of detection, he found different functions in different areas of the brain's surface — an exciting discovery decades ago! I'm not sure if you're going to be able to do anything with your left hand, but you're going to be able to do it with your left hand. Another point may give you a feeling, for example, flash; Some of the excitement brings back memories of childhood sometimes (Penfield, 1959); Penfield & Baldwin, 1952. Later, other scientists followed closely to explore deeper structures of the brain. Researchers have found that electric stimulation can trigger a complex set of behaviours or emotions. The conclusions of this series of studies are clear: each brain region has its own specific function.

p29.original: 在过去的几十年中，统称为脑部扫描的精密技术使得我们对脑的了解越来越详细。有些扫描技术使用X射线成像，另一些使用放射性示踪剂，还有一些利用了磁场。现在，科学家可以在不打开颅骨的情况下拍摄到生动的、功能正常的脑结构图。
p29.en: Over the past few decades, precision technology, collectively known as brain scans, has led to a more detailed understanding of the brain. Some scanning techniques use X-ray imaging, others use radioactive tracers and others use magnetic fields. Now, scientists can take a live, functional brain structure without opening the skull.

p30.original: 在医学上，脑部扫描可以帮助神经外科医生定位脑部出现异常的位置，例如，肿瘤或中风。在心理学中，通过脑部扫描获得的图片可以揭示我们加工思想和感受的位置。那么如何做呢？根据所使用的扫描方法，当一个人阅读、说话、解决问题或体会到某种情绪时特定的脑区就会被“点亮”（Raichle，1994）。
p30.en: Medically, brain scans can help neurosurgeons to locate brain abnormalities, such as tumors or strokes. In psychology, images obtained through brain scans reveal where we process thoughts and feelings. So how do we do it? According to the scanning method used, a particular brain zone is “lighted” when a person reads, talks, solves a problem or feels an emotion (Raichle, 1994).

p31.original: 目前最常见的脑部扫描方法有CT、PET、MRI和fMRI（见图2-9）。
p31.en: The most common methods of brain scanning are currently CT, PET, MRI and fMRI (see figures 2-9).

p33.original: 注：多种脑部扫描技术可用于测量和研究脑部活动。每一种方法都采用一种特定的技术手段，因此也具有与这种方法相关的独特优势。
p33.en: Note: Multiple brain scanning techniques can be used to measure and study brain activity. Each approach uses a specific technical tool and therefore has unique advantages associated with it.

p35.original: 每种脑部扫描方法都有其优缺点。CT扫描成像质量好，相对成本较低，经常是评估内伤，特别是脑损伤的首选扫描方法。PET扫描现在被用来识别人们脑中的斑块（一种互相交织的“死”细胞簇，它可能是阿尔茨海默病的症状）。这为这种疾病的早期诊断提供了新的机会。fMRI可以揭示在某项特定的任务（例如，说话、看图或解决问题）中脑活动的具体脑区，这种方法在定位特定认知功能的研究中的优势非常明显。就其本身而言，标准的MRI擅长区分脑结构的精细细节，因此它可以帮助神经科医生寻找功能障碍的证据。
p35.en: Each method of brain scanning has its advantages and disadvantages. CT scans are of good quality and relatively low cost and are often the preferred scanning method for assessing internal injuries, especially brain damage. PET scans are now used to identify spots in people's minds (a interwoven “dead” cell cluster, which may be symptoms of Alzheimer's disease). This offers new opportunities for early diagnosis of the disease. fMRI can reveal the specific brain area of brain activity in a given mission (e.g. speaking, viewing or problem solving), an approach that has a clear advantage in the study of the location of a given cognitive function. For its part, the standard MRI is very good at distinguishing the precise details of brain structure, so it can help neurologists to find evidence of dysfunction.

p36.original: 然而，需要注意的是，脑部扫描并不能百分之百准确地出具身体和心理状况的诊断。多数时候，它们可以排除某些疾病，或提供一些有助于诊断的证据。因此，它们应该被看成是医生和神经科学家工具箱中非常有用的工具，它们是必要的，但是对更深入的研究来说还不够充分。
p36.en: It should be noted, however, that brain scans do not provide 100 per cent accurate diagnosis of physical and psychological conditions. Most of the time, they can exclude certain diseases or provide some evidence that will help to diagnose them. They should therefore be seen as very useful tools in the toolbox for doctors and neuroscientists, which are necessary but not sufficient for more in-depth research.

p37.original: 随着神经成像技术的不断进步，大家可以持续关注它们的进展。
p37.en: As neuroimaging technologies continue to progress, you can follow their progress on a continuous basis.

p38.en: 2.8 Three-tier structure of the human brain

p40.original: 解释脑干、边缘系统和大脑皮层的作用。
p40.en: Explain the role of brain stem, peripheral system and cerebral cortex.

p41.original: 当然，不同的脑各有差异。但是大象的脑、蜜蜂的脑和人脑有什么区别呢？脑的尺寸重要吗？鸟类和爬行动物的生存依靠的是一个比根茎还小的脑，它们的脑会调节最基本的生命过程和本能反应。我们更加复杂的脑也源自于相似的茎，被称为脑干。从进化的角度来看，这是人脑中最古老的祖先，它们负责最基本的功能。在那根茎的上面，我们和我们的表亲哺乳动物进化出了两层脑结构，被称为边缘系统（limbic system）和大脑（cerebrum），这极大地增加了我们的脑的能力（见图2-10）。
p41.en: Of course, different brains are different. But what difference does it make between the brain of an elephant, the brain of a bee and the human brain? Does the brain size matter? Birds and reptiles rely on a brain smaller than the root, which regulates the most basic life processes and instincts. Our more complex brain is also derived from a similar penis, called brain stem. From an evolutionary point of view, this is the oldest ancestor in the human mind, who are responsible for the most basic functions. Above that root, we and our cousin mammals evolved two layers of brain structure, known as limbic system and cerebrum, which greatly increased our brain capacity (see figures 2-10).

p42.en: Figure 2-10 Main structure of the brain

p43.original: 注：从进化的角度看，脑干和小脑是人脑最古老的部分，然后是边缘系统，大脑皮层是最后进化获得的。
p43.en: Note: From an evolutionary point of view, brain stem and small brain are the oldest parts of the human brain, followed by the peripheral system, and the cortex of the brain is the last to evolve.

p44.original: 这两层脑结构在调节我们的功能方面发挥了哪些作用？每一层脑组织各具有哪些特殊结构可以帮助我们完成哪些任务？
p44.en: What role do these two layers of brain structures play in regulating our functions? What are the special structures of each layer of brain tissue that can help us to accomplish?

p46.original: 如果你曾在无聊的课堂上（或者通宵工作了一个晚上后）努力保持清醒，那么你肯定在跟你的脑干较劲。不过，在多数情况下，脑干在默不作声地执行维持生命的工作，并不令人讨厌。我们可以从脑干的位置推断出它的一项功能：连接脊髓和脑。作为神经通路的管道，它通过身体和脑之间的脊髓长廊上下传递信息。它也是感觉和运动通路，连接脑和对侧的感觉器官与骨骼肌，也就是说，脑的每一个半球和对侧身体相连（对侧通路）。
p46.en: If you've tried to stay awake in a boring class (or working all night after all night), you're definitely doing something with your brain. In most cases, however, it is not undesirable that the brain stem carries out life-sustaining work in silence. We can deduce one of its functions from the brain stem position: connect the spinal cord to the brain. As a conduit for the neuropath, it conveys information through the spinal lobes between the body and the brain. It also connects feelings and motion, connects brain and side-to-side sensory organs to bone muscles, that is, the individual hemisphere of the brain and the side-to-side body (to side-to-side routes).

p47.original: 然而，脑干不仅仅是一个管道，它也将几个重要的信息处理区域连接起来，其中三个区域（延髓、脑桥和网状结构）包含在脑干之中，另外两个紧邻脑干（丘脑和小脑）（Pinel，2005）。从进化的角度来看，这些组织结构非常古老，各种不同动物的脑中都有，包括企鹅、熊猫、蟒蛇、豪猪和人类。你可以从图2-11中看到它们的位置结构。
p47.en: However, the brain stem is not just a conduit, but it also connects several important information processing areas, three of which are contained in the brain stem (marrow, brain bridge and mesh structure) and the other two that are closely connected to the brain stem (pune and small brain) (Pinel, 2005). From an evolutionary point of view, these structures are very old and are found in the minds of a variety of animals, including penguins, pandas, python, porcupines, hogs and humans. You can see their position structure in figures 2-11.

p48.original: 图2-11 脑干和它周围的神经组织
p48.en: Charts 2-11 Brain stem and the nervous tissue around it

p49.original: 注：从图中，你可以看到脑干，网状结构垂直穿过它，延髓和脑桥位于中上部。小脑在脑干后面，丘脑在上面。
p49.en: Note: From the figure, you can see brain stem, a web structure that cuts vertically through it, with membranes and brain bridges in the upper middle. The little brain is behind the stem of the brain, the dome is on it.

p50.original: 延髓（medulla）是脑干上面的一个凸起，它负责调节基本的身体功能，包括呼吸、血压和心率。它的工作模式是“自动驾驶”——不需要意识的参与就可以维持我们内部器官的运转。
p50.en: The medulla is a condensation of the brain stem, which regulates basic physical functions, including breathing, blood pressure and heart rate. It works in the form of "automated driving" — without conscious participation to sustain the functioning of our internal organs.

p51.original: 延髓的上方有一个更大的凸起，那是脑桥（pons），它内部的神经回路可以调节睡眠和做梦周期。顾名思义，脑桥也充当脑干和小脑（参与协调运动）的“桥梁”。
p51.en: There's a bigger bulge on the upper end of the marrow, which is the pens, which regulates the sleep and the dream cycle through the internal nervous circuit. By definition, brain bridges also serve as “bridges” for brain stem and small brain (involved in coordinated campaigns).

p52.original: 贯穿整个脑干中心的是网状结构（reticular formation），它是铅笔形状的神经细胞束，构成了整个脑干的核心。网状结构的功能之一是保持大脑的清醒和警觉。其他功能包括监控输入的感觉信息流并将注意指向新信息或重要信息。因此，不要责怪你的教授讲课讲得不好，让你在课堂上昏昏欲睡的是你的网状结构。
p52.en: The entire brain stem is a network structure (reticular formation), which is a neurocell beam in the shape of a pencil and forms the core of the entire brain stem. One of the functions of a network structure is to keep the brain awake and alert. Other functions include monitoring the input of sensor flow and pointing attention to new or important information. So, let's not blame your professor for his poor lecture, and what makes you sleepy in class is your web structure.

p53.original: 丘脑（thalamus）是位于脑干上部的一对橄榄球状的神经组织，它接收来自于网状结构的神经纤维。从功能上看，丘脑更像是大脑半球的一部分而不是脑干的附属组织，它像一台计算机的中央处理器，指挥人脑中的输入感觉信息流和输出运动信息流的方向。因此，它接收（除了嗅觉之外的）所有的感觉信息并将它们分发到脑中适宜的加工回路。
p53.en: The thalamus is a pair of football-like neurosynthetic tissues located on the upper end of the brain, which receives neurofibre from a mesh structure. Functionally, the dome is more like a part of the brain hemisphere than an affiliate of brain stem, and it is like a central processor for a computer, directing the direction of the flow of input and output flow of information in the human brain. Thus, it receives (except for smell) all sensory information and distributes them to the proper processing circuits in its brain.

p54.original: 最后一个组织是小脑（cerebellum），它藏在大脑半球的下面，脑干的后面。它的形状看起来非常像一个小号的大脑——事实上，它的名字来自于拉丁语“小的脑”。小脑的体积大约是整个人脑的10%。小脑密集地布满了神经元——事实上，它包含了整个脑的50%的神经元。这个丰富的神经网络可能可以解释关于小脑功能的一些惊人的发现。虽然长期以来，人们认为它只负责运动协调和平衡（Spencer et al.，2003；Wickelgren，1998），现在神经学家发现小脑在感觉、空间、情绪和认知功能中也有作用。因此，小脑不仅可以在你骑车、打棒球或跑下楼梯时帮助你无意识地、精确地移动你的脚，它也能帮你阅读GPS扫描结果、提前规划、记忆和进行有技巧的谈话（Schmahmann，2010；Schmahmann & Caplan，2006）。小脑通过与大脑其他区域的广泛连接网络，促进了与大脑其他部分相关的各种任务。
p54.en: The last tissue is cerebellum, hidden beneath the hemisphere of the brain, behind the stem of the brain. It looks very much like a small brain -- in fact, its name comes from the Latin word "small brain." The size of the small brain is about 10 per cent of the human brain. The small brain is densely covered in neurons -- in fact, it contains 50% of the neurons of the entire brain. This rich neural network may explain some of the amazing discoveries about the functioning of the small brain. Although it has long been considered responsible only for sports coordination and balance (Spencer et al., 2003); Wickelgren, 1998), neurologists now find that the brain also plays a role in sensory, spatial, emotional and cognitive functions. So, the brain not only helps you move your feet unconsciously and precisely when you ride, play baseball or run down the stairs, it also helps you read GPS scan results, advance planning, memory and skillful conversations (Schmahmann, 2010); Schmahmann & Caplan, 2006. The small brain promotes tasks related to other parts of the brain through a wide network of connections to other regions of the brain.

p55.original: 小脑功能的主要研究人员神经学家杰里米·施马曼（Jeremy Schmahmann）认为，小脑本质上是所有这些活动的“精细调节器”。我们早已知道，当小脑功能失常时，一个人可能还可以走路，但是他的动作不连贯，非常笨拙，而且难以保持平衡。我们现在知道小脑在我们的思维和情绪中起着相似的作用，帮助我们的思维保持流畅和有条理，使我们能及时做出反应，并且使我们的情绪适宜我们的社会情境。这种联系的证据来自于小脑损伤的个体——包括精神分裂症患者，他们经常在这些功能上存在缺陷。因此，研究人员正在考察小脑损伤是否是精神分裂症背后的原因（Okugawa，2013）。这个脑结构也会帮助我们了解环境刺激和反射行为之间的联系，例如，你在诊所看到针头时就会害怕（Hazeltine & Ivry，2002；Thompson & Steinmetz，2009）。
p55.en: Jeremy Schmahmann, the leading neuralist in the brain function, believes that the brain is essentially a “better regulator” for all of these activities. We already know that when a small brain is dysfunctional, a person may still be able to walk, but his actions are incoherent, very clumsy and difficult to balance. We now know that the small brain plays a similar role in our thinking and emotions, helping us to keep our thinking fluid and structured, enabling us to react in a timely manner and adapting our emotions to our social context. Evidence of this connection is given by individuals with small brain damage, including schizophrenia, who often suffer from functional deficiencies. As a result, researchers are examining whether the small brain damage is behind schizophrenia (Okugawa, 2013). This brain structure will also help us understand the link between environmental irritation and reflective behaviour, for example, when you see needles in a clinic (Hazeltine & Ivry, 2002); Thompson & Steinmetz, 2009.

p56.original: 总之，脑干和它的邻居控制着运动和生命的最基本的大多数功能。再次提醒一下，它们的大多数功能都是自动化的，不需要意识的参与。然而，人脑的另外两层会更明显地出现在意识中（见图2-12）。
p56.en: In short, brain stem and its neighbours control most of the most basic functions of sport and life. Again, most of their functions are automated and do not require conscious participation. However, two other layers of the human brain are more visible in consciousness (see figures 2-12).

p57.original: 图2-12 脑干和它周围神经组织的结构和功能
p57.en: Charts 2-12: Brain stem and the structure and function of the nervous tissue around it

p58.original: 注：回顾你学过的脑的结构，并且总结其关键功能。
p58.en: Note: Review the structure of the brain you have learned and summarize its key functions.

p59.original: 2.8.2 边缘系统：情绪、记忆及其他
p59.en: 2.8.2 Marginal systems: Emotions, memory and others

p60.original: 我们很遗憾地告诉你，你的宠物金丝雀或漂亮的金鱼并没有与我们哺乳动物类似的情绪“装置”。你看，只有哺乳动物才有一个发育完全的边缘系统，它是围绕着丘脑的一些结构的集合，它位于大脑半球的深处，脑干的顶部（见图2-13）。
p60.en: We regret to tell you that your pet canary or beautiful goldfish do not have an emotional “set” similar to our mammals. You see, only mammals have a fully developed peripheral system, which is a collection of structures around the dome, which is located deep in the hemisphere of the brain at the top of its stem (see figures 2-13).

p62.original: 注：边缘系统参与动机、情绪和某些记忆的加工。
p62.en: Note: Marginalized systems are involved in the processing of motivations, emotions and certain memories.

p63.original: 这些羊角状的结构大大增强了我们的情绪和记忆能力，使我们拥有了心理灵活性这一巨大优势。因为有边缘系统，我们不需要像低级动物一样，行为完全依赖本能和反射。
p63.en: The structure of these horns has greatly enhanced our emotional and memory abilities and has given us the enormous advantage of psychological flexibility. Because of the peripheral system, we don't need to act like low-level animals, relying entirely on instinct and reflection.

p64.original: 边缘系统也包含了其他一些模块，例如，调节饥饿、口渴和体温等过程。总体来说，边缘系统是人脑控制情绪、动机、记忆和保持身体平衡的“指挥所”。下面让我们仔细了解它的每一个模块及其相应的功能。
p64.en: Marginal systems also contain other modules, such as regulating the processes of hunger, thirst and body temperature. In general, the peripheral system is a “commanding post” for brain control of emotions, motivations, memories and body balance. Let's take a closer look at each of its modules and their respective functions.

p66.original: 海马（hippocampus）是我们的记忆系统，它在500年前因为形状像海洋动物海马而得名。脑的每一侧都有一个海马，一共有两个海马（见图2-12）。海马的一个任务是帮助我们记住物体的位置，例如，你把车子停在了一个大停车场的哪个位置（Squire，2007）。海马似乎会随经验的增加而长大。一项针对伦敦出租车司机的研究发现，出租车司机的海马比不开出租车的普通人更大，而且司机的经验越多，他的海马就越大（Maguire et al.，2003）。
p66.en: The hippocampus is our memory system, which was famous 500 years ago for being shaped like a marine animal. Each side of the brain has one seahorse, with a total of two seahorses (see figures 2-12). One of the tasks of the hippo is to help us remember the location of the object, for example, where you parked the car in a large parking lot (Squire, 2007). Seahorses seem to grow up with experience. A study of taxi drivers in London found that taxi drivers had more sea horses than ordinary people who did not drive taxis, and that the more experienced the driver, the larger his sea horses (Maguire et al., 2003).

p67.original: 除了空间记忆外，海马对记忆存储也起到关键作用。例如，亨利·莫莱森（HenryMolaison）的悲惨故事证明了这一点。亨利·莫莱森更广为人知的名字是H.M.（为了保护他的隐私，在他生前，别人都用首字母来称呼他）。1953年，当时H.M.二十刚出头，为了治疗已经威胁到他生命的频繁发作的癫痫，他接受了一项激进的、实验性的脑手术（Hilts，1995）。这项手术切除了他的脑两侧的大部分海马，成功减少了癫痫发作的次数。不幸的是，这项手术也产生了一个不可预测的、灾难性的副作用：手术之后，新的经历在事情发生之后就会立即从他的记忆中消失，但他对手术之前的事情的记忆完好无损。在他的余生中，当他试图回忆1953年之后的事情时，得到的是一片空白。他甚至不能记住每天照顾他的人。直到2008年去世之前，他还相信自己活在1953年。这个故事以及其他确凿证据表明，虽然海马不是记忆存储的地方，但是它对于创造新的记忆至关重要。
p67.en: In addition to space memory, sea horses play a key role in memory storage. The tragic story of Henry Molaison, for example, bears witness to this. Henry Møllison's more widely known name is H.M. (in order to protect his privacy, he was called in his initials before he was born). In 1953, when H.M. had just arrived, he had undergone a radical, experimental brain surgery to treat the frequent epilepsy that had threatened his life (Hilts, 1995). The operation, which removed most of the hippos on both sides of his brain, succeeded in reducing the number of epilepsy seizures. Unfortunately, the operation also produced an unpredictable and disastrous side effect: after the operation, new experiences would disappear from his memory immediately after the event, but his memory of what happened before the operation was intact. For the rest of his life, when he tried to remember what had happened after 1953, he had been left with a blank. He can't even remember the people who take care of him every day. Until his death in 2008, he believed he lived in 1953. This story and other hard evidence show that, while the hippos are not places where memories are stored, they are essential for the creation of new memories.

p68.original: 海马（左右半球各有一个）对于创建新的记忆至关重要，在空间记忆方面也起关键作用。
p68.en: Seahorses (one each in the right and the right hemispheres) are essential for the creation of new memories and play a key role in spatial memory.

p70.original: 另一个边缘系统的组成部分是杏仁核（amygdala），它的名字也来自于它的形状，在希腊语中的意思是“杏仁”。和其他脑结构一样，杏仁核也有两个，位于双侧海马的前面（见图2-12）。
p70.en: Another component of the peripheral system is amygdala, whose name also comes from its shape, meaning “almonds” in Greek. Like other brain structures, almonds have two cores, located in front of the bipolar seahorse (see figures 2-12).

p71.original: 为了了解杏仁核的功能，海因里希·克鲁弗（HeinrichKlüver）和保罗·布西（PaulBucy）（1939）设计了一项经典的实验，采用外科手术切断了脾气暴躁的恒河猴的双侧杏仁核之间的连接。术后，这些动物变得非常温顺，连克鲁弗和布西都感到非常吃惊。他们的发现首次清晰地证明了杏仁核在恐惧和攻击性中的作用。当我们感到威胁时，这个脑结构会变得特别活跃，它在我们应对恐惧时起着关键作用。
p71.en: In order to understand the function of almond cores, Heinrich Klüver and Paul Bacy (1939) designed a classic experiment to use surgical operations to cut off the connection between the apricotal nuclei of the grumpy rhesus monkeys. After the operation, the animals became very gentle, and even Crover and Bussi were surprised. Their discovery clearly demonstrated for the first time the role of almonds in fear and aggression. This brain structure becomes particularly active when we feel threatened, and it plays a key role in our response to fear.

p72.original: 杏仁核（和大多数脑结构一样，我们实际上有两个杏仁核，每个半球一个）在恐惧和其他与生存相关的情绪中起关键作用。它位于海马前面。它的两个部分互相调节，使用记忆来校准情绪反应。
p72.en: Almond cores (like most brain structures, we actually have two almonds, one in each hemisphere) play a key role in fear and other survival-related emotions. It's in front of the sea horse. Its two components are mutually adjusted, and memory is used to calibrate emotional responses.

p73.original: 近期的研究拓展了我们对杏仁核的认识。例如，杏仁核会和海马协同工作，这样对先前经验的记忆就会帮助我们矫正当前的情绪反应（Roozendaal et al.，2009）。例如，一个曾在车祸中受伤的人可能会对其他司机做出的一个小小的威胁（例如，尾随）表现得反应过度。这可以解释创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的一些负向触发反应。当男性和女性观看性唤起图片时，杏仁核也会活跃起来（男性的活跃程度更高）（Hamann，2005），这表明杏仁核不仅参与了消极情绪反应，也参与了积极情绪加工。杏仁核还被认为是在孤独症谱系障碍（autism spectrum disorders）中起作用的几个脑结构之一，例如，孤独症个体的杏仁核通常较大（Baron-Cohen et al.，2000）。
p73.en: Recent research has expanded our understanding of almond cores. For example, almonds work with sea horses, so that memory of previous experience helps us to correct current emotional reactions (Roozendaal et al., 2009). For example, a person who had been injured in a car accident may have over-reacted a minor threat (e.g., tailing) to other drivers. This explains some negative-directive triggers for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). When men and women watch sex calls pictures, almond cores become active (males are more active) (Hamann, 2005), indicating that almond cores are involved not only in negative emotional reactions but also in active emotional processing. Almond cores are also considered to be one of several brain structures working in autism spectrum disorders, for example, the almond cores of autism individuals are usually larger (Baron-Cohen et al., 2000).

p75.original: 我们曾在前面谈到过下丘脑（hypothalamus）（hypo在希腊语中是下面的意思，所以这个名字告诉我们它的位置在丘脑的下面）。它是边缘系统中保持身体处于稳定、平衡状态的结构。这一功能部分是通过启动内分泌系统信息实现的。你可能记得在健康或生物课上学过这一过程，它叫作内稳态（homeostasis）。下丘脑富含血液和神经元，因此它的功能之一是充当脑血液分析实验室。通过对血液的持续监测，它可以探测体温、血流水平和营养物质的微小变化。当它发现某种不平衡（例如，水太多或者水太少）时，下丘脑会立刻发出命令来设法恢复平衡。
p75.en: We have spoken before about hypothalamus (hypo in Greek means the following, so the name tells us that it's underneath the hypocus). It is the structure of the peripheral system that maintains a stable and balanced body. This function was partially achieved by initiating endocrine system information. You may remember this process in health or biology, called homeostasis. The hypothalamus is rich in blood and neurons, so one of its functions is to act as a laboratory for brain blood analysis. Through continuous blood monitoring, it can detect minor changes in body temperature, blood flow levels and nutrients. When it discovers some imbalance (e.g., too much water or too little water), the hypodermic is immediately ordered to try to restore the balance.

p76.original: 下丘脑还是脑的快乐中枢或奖赏回路，它会产生由饮食、性或其他药物引起的积极情绪（Olds & Fobes，1981；Pinel，2005）。另一些活动也能刺激边缘系统的快乐回路，包括幽默、坐过山车之类的刺激活动，甚至品尝味道浓郁的巧克力（Small et al.，2001；Watson et al.，2007）。
p76.en: The hypothalamus is also a joy centre or reward route for the brain, which produces positive emotions caused by diet, sex or other drugs (Olds & Fobes, 1981); Pinel, 2005. Other activities can also stimulate the happy return of peripheral systems, including humor, roller coasters, etc., and even taste the lavish chocolate (Small et al., 2001); Watson et al., 2007).

p77.original: 多巴胺是在这些快乐回路中起关键作用的几种神经递质之一。每一次我们投入一项愉快的活动中去时，多巴胺就会被释放出来，使我们感觉良好，这样我们就会渴望再尝试一次（无论对象是食物、性、药物或其他任何东西），以获得同样的“快感”。这些进化而来的奖赏中枢激励我们做出有利于生存的行为。然而，滥用药物也会以相同的方式刺激我们的奖赏中枢，并且它们会更加有效。因此，滥用药物可能会劫持具有成瘾倾向的个体的奖赏回路，刺激他们去寻求更多的药物，同时忽略竞争性的生物需求（Volkow et al.，2010）。
p77.en: Dopamine is one of several neurotransmitters that play a key role in these happy circuits. Every time we go into a pleasant activity, dopamine is released, making us feel good, so that we are eager to try again (whether for food, sex, medicine or anything) to get the same “favourable”. These evolutionary reward hubs inspire us to act in the interest of survival. However, drug abuse can also stimulate our reward centres in the same way and they can be more effective. As a result, substance abuse may hijack reward routes for addictive individuals, stimulating them to seek more drugs while ignoring competitive biological needs (Volkow et al., 2010).

p78.original: 下丘脑也会以其他方式产生影响。虽然它的很多工作都是在无意识状态下进行的，下丘脑也将神经信息发送到“更高级”的加工脑区，使我们意识到它的需求（例如，感到饥饿）。它也会通过对垂体的影响来控制我们的内部器官，垂体位于脑底部下丘脑的下方。因此，下丘脑充当着神经系统和内分泌系统的纽带来调节情绪唤起和应激。
p78.en: The hypothalamus can have an effect in other ways. Although much of its work is carried out in a state of unconsciousness, the hypochondriac also sends neural messages to the “higher” processing brain zone, making us aware of its needs (e.g., feeling hungry). It also controls our internal organs through its effects on the pituitary, which lies below the lower end of the hypodermic. Thus, the hypothalamus acts as a link between the nervous and endocrine systems to regulate emotional agitation and stress.

p79.original: 2.8.3 大脑皮层：人脑的思考帽
p79.en: 2.8.3 Brain cortex: human brain thinking caps

p80.original: 当你观察整个人脑的时候，你看到的大部分是凸起的大脑半球——它比你握紧贴在一起的两个拳头大一点。你可能会注意到它们被一条称为“胼胝体”（corpus callosum）的纤维束连接在一起，两个半球通过胼胝体进行沟通。近乎对称的两个半球包括厚厚的一层（被称为大脑，这部分的质量约为人脑的三分之二），以及大部分边缘系统。大脑最外面薄薄的一层是大脑皮层（cerebral cortex），它是人脑的思考帽：它独特的褶皱表面使得超过100亿的神经元可以聚集在几毫米的厚度中。如果把褶皱摊平，皮层表面大约有一张打开的报纸那么大。但是由于其表面卷曲盘绕，我们只能看到大约三分之一的皮层。
p80.en: When you look at the whole human brain, most of what you see is the condensed hemisphere of the brain -- it's a little bit bigger than the two fists you hold together. You may note that they are connected by a fibre beam called the Corpus callusum, which communicates between the two hemispheres. The near symmetrical two hemispheres consist of a thick layer (known as the brain, which is about two thirds of the mass of the human brain) and most peripheral systems. The thinest layer of the brain is the cerebral cottex, which is the head of the human brain: its unique wrinkled surface allows more than 10 billion neurons to gather in a few millimeters of thickness. If the wrinkles were spread, the surface of the cortex was about one open newspaper as big as that. But because of its surface curly, we can only see about one third of the cortex.

p81.original: 一个健康的人脑分成两半，这样就露出了脑表面的回（凸起）和沟（凹陷）。这些沟回形成的褶皱可以使数十亿的脑细胞挤进很小的一个区域。
p81.en: A healthy human brain is split in half, so that the brain surface returns (crumbs) and ditches (deepness). These gutters are corroded to squeeze billions of brain cells into a small area.

p82.original: 大脑皮层有什么功能呢？它就是内在的你！它是我们最强大的心理力量所在的地方，它加工我们所有的感觉，存储记忆，并且做出决策。它还有很多其他功能，我们在后续小节中讨论大脑各个脑区时会介绍这些功能。
p82.en: What does the cortex do? It's the inside of you! It is where our most powerful psychological power lies, processing all our feelings, storing memories and making decisions. It has many other functions that we will introduce in the next section when we discuss the various brain regions of the brain.

p83.original: 虽然我们人类为我们的“大”脑感到自豪，但是实际上，我们的脑并不是这个星球上最大的脑。所有大型动物的脑都很大——事实上相比于智力，脑的大小与体型的关系更密切。有褶皱的皮层也不是人类特有的。所有大型动物的皮层都是卷曲盘绕的。也许这伤害了你的自尊，但请放轻松一点，相对于我们的体重来说，我们的大脑皮层要比其他拥有脑的生物大得多。虽然没有人知道为什么人类的脑会如此大，以及它是怎么变得这么大的（Buss，2008；Pennisi，2006），但相比于其他动物，人类的独特性在于我们的脑的运作方式而不是大小。值得一提的是，女性的脑比男性拥有更多的褶皱，而男性的脑平均而言比女性更大（Luders et al.，2004）。
p83.en: While we human beings are proud of our “big” brain, in fact, our brain is not the largest brain on this planet. All macrofauna have large brains - in fact, brain size is more closely related to body size than intellectual. Wrinkled cortex is not unique to humans. The cortex of all macrofauna is cortexed. Maybe it hurts your self-esteem, but just relax, we have a much larger brain cortex than any other brain-bearing creature. Although no one knows why the human brain is so big and how it's gotten so big (Buss, 2008); Pennisi, 2006), but compared to other animals, the uniqueness of humans lies in the way our brains work, not in their size. It is worth mentioning that women have more wrinkles than men, while men have more women on average (Luders et al., 2004).

p86.original: 区分大脑皮层的每一个脑叶的独特功能。
p86.en: Distinguishing the unique function of each leaf in the cortex of the brain.

p87.original: 18世纪90年代后期，著名的奥地利医生弗朗茨·约瑟夫·加尔（Franz Joseph Gall）将自己的科研重心放在一个理论上，该理论提出大脑的特定脑区控制特定的心理功能，例如，听、说、运动、视觉和记忆。但是，他把这个很明智的理论推向了极端：在他的颅相学（phrenology）中，加尔声称脑也有专门用于灵性、希望、仁慈、友谊、毁灭和谨慎等特质的区域。并且，他声称这些特质可以通过颅骨上的凸起检测出来，于是催生了一个“读取”这些特质的小型诈骗行业。在19世纪30年代，包括哈佛教授在内的成千上万的人涌进颅相学讲座，很多人付费来“看”自己的颅像，他们会把这些结果用于做出人际关系、职业，甚至招聘等方面的决定。
p87.en: In the late 1990s, the famous Austrian doctor Franz Joseph Gall focused his research on the theory that specific brain areas controlled specific mental functions, such as hearing, speaking, exercise, vision and memory. But he pushed this wise theory to the extreme: in his phrenology, Gale claimed that the brain also had a region dedicated to spirituality, hope, mercy, friendship, destruction and prudence. Moreover, he claims that these traits can be detected by the concussion of the skull, which led to the creation of a small fraud industry that “reads” these traits. In the 1930s, thousands of people, including Harvard Professors, came to the cranial lecture, and many paid to “see” their skulls, and they used them to make decisions about relationships, careers, and even recruitment.

p88.original: 加尔的观点引起了公众的关注，并且非常受欢迎，即使这个理论大部分都是错误的。然而，在一个重要的观点上，他是绝对正确的：功能定位学说，即大脑不同的部分执行不同的任务。现代神经科学的发现证实了这一观点，并帮助我们修正了加尔关于大脑皮层错误的看法。我们现在对大脑皮层的主要功能有了更准确的理解（见图2-14）。
p88.en: The Gar's point of view has attracted public attention and is very popular, even though most of this theory is wrong. However, he is absolutely right on an important point: the functional positioning doctrine, i.e. the different parts of the brain perform different tasks. The discovery of modern neuroscience confirms this view and helps us to correct Gale's perception of the brain cortex error. We now have a more accurate understanding of the main functions of the cortex of the brain (see figures 2-14).

p90.original: 注：虽然颅相学被证实是伪科学，但是脑的不同区域具有不同的功能这种观点是正确的。
p90.en: Note: Although craniology has been proven to be pseudo-science, it is true that different regions of the brain have different functions.

p92.original: 你选择的专业，你的暑期计划和你处理课程的能力，你的工作和你的个人生活在很大部分上依赖于脑前面的皮层区域，它被命名为额叶（frontal lobes，每个半球都有一个，见图2-15）。
p92.en: Your choice of profession, your summer plans and your ability to handle the course, your work and your personal lives in a cortical area that is largely dependent on the front of the brain, and is named the frontal lobe (one in every hemisphere, see figs. 2-15).

p93.original: 图2-15 大脑皮层的4个脑叶
p93.en: Figure 2-15: 4 brain leaves in the cortex of the brain

p94.original: 最前面的区域被称为前额皮层（prefrontal cortex）。前额皮层的神经回路承担着我们最高级的心理功能——执行功能（executive functions），例如，决策、目标设定和跟进、未来预测等（Miller，2006）。正如菲尼亚斯·盖奇的案例所展示的那样，人格、气质和“自我”意识等心理特质的生物学基础也在这里（Bower，2006）。前额皮层对于“人之所以为人”有着重要的作用。
p94.en: The most advanced area is known as prefrontal cortex. The frontal cortex's nerve circuit carries with it our most advanced mental function - executive functions, such as decision-making, targeting and follow-up, future predictions, etc. (Miller, 2006). As the case of Finyas Gage illustrates, the biological basis of psychological characteristics such as personality, abstem and “self” consciousness is here (Bower, 2006). The frontal cortex plays an important role in “human beings”.

p95.original: 前额皮层的后面有一块条状的特殊皮层，它能将我们的思想转化为行动。这就是运动皮层（motor cortex），这块脑区的名字来自于它的主要功能：通过给运动神经和随意肌发送信号来控制躯体运动。正如你在图2-16所看到的，运动皮层包含了一个上下颠倒的身体映射，我们用一个小矮人来表示（见图中扭曲的“小人”）。
p95.en: The front cortex is followed by a special cortex of strips that translates our thinking into action. This is the motor cortex, the name of which comes from its main function: to control body movement by sending signals to motor nerves and random muscles. As you can see in figures 2-16, the sports cortex contains a upside-down body map, which we use as a dwarf (see the distorted “minor”).

p96.original: 仔细观察这个运动小矮人，你会发现，其身体的某些部分被放大了，这表明脑将更大的皮层区域分配给了这些需要精细运动控制的身体部件，例如，嘴唇、舌头和手。最夸张的区域表征的是手指（特别是拇指），这可能反映了操控物体的重要性。另一个大区域和面部肌肉相联系，被用于表达情绪。不过，还记得对侧加工吗？因此，你的左眼眨一下源于右侧运动皮层，而你的左侧运动皮层则可以让你眨右眼。
p96.en: Looking closely at this sported dwarf, you will find that some parts of his body have been amplified, which suggests that the larger cortex area is allocated to those parts of the body that require fine motion control, such as lips, tongues and hands. The most exaggerated regional expression is the finger (especially the thumb), which may reflect the importance of manipulating objects. Another large area is linked to facial muscles, which are used to express emotions. But remember the side processing? So, your left eye blinks from the right side of the motion cortex, and your left side of the cortex allows you to blink.

p97.original: 左前额皮层在语言中的作用
p97.en: Role of the left front cortex in language

p98.original: 对大多数人而言，左前额皮层的另一个重要功能是产生语言（见图2-15）。这个特异性区域是由19世纪中叶的法国神经学家保罗·布洛卡（Paul Broca）首次发现的。因此，这个区域被命名为“布洛卡区”。一个人的布洛卡区受损会使他失去说话的能力。你可能已经猜到了，吉尔·波特·泰勒的中风导致她的布洛卡区受损，这就是她失去了说话能力的原因。但是，理解语言的能力却源于人脑的其他地方。
p98.en: For most people, another important function of the left front cortex is to produce language (see figure 2-15). This particular region was first discovered by the French neurologist Paul Broca in the mid-19th century. As a result, the area was named “Broka district”. The damage to a person's Broka district would deprive him of his ability to speak. You may have guessed that Jill Potter Taylor's stroke caused damage to her Brokah district, which is why she lost her ability to speak. However, the ability to understand languages stems from other parts of the human brain.

p99.original: 图2-16 运动皮层和躯体感觉皮层
p99.en: Figure 2-16: Sporting cortex and body cortex

p100.original: 布洛卡区位于额叶左侧，它对于语言的产生至关重要，但是它与口语或手势（如美国手语）等语言表达无关。
p100.en: The Brocka district, which is on the left side of the forehead, is essential for the production of languages, but it has nothing to do with language expressions such as spoken language or signage (e.g., United States sign language).

p101.original: 前额皮层中的镜像神经元
p101.en: Mirror neurons in the front cortex.

p102.original: 在20世纪90年代后期，神经科学家研究恒河猴的脑时，发现了一类新的神经元，被称为镜像神经元（mirror neurons），位于恒河猴的脑的运动区。当一只猴子观察到另一只猴子在进行目标导向的行为（例如，从盒子里拿出一个苹果或用杯子喝水）时，它的镜像神经元会放电，就好像观察者自己也完成了这个动作一样。实际上，观察猴的脑正在“镜像”它观察到的这个动作。由于灵长类动物的脑与人类的大脑在很多方面非常相似，这项发现引导科学家对人类镜像神经元的作用进行了大量的预测。一位著名的科学家甚至预测镜像神经元对于心理学的意义就像DNA的发现对于生物学的意义一样（Ramachandran，2000）！但是，我们有多少证据支持这些想法呢？
p102.en: In the late 1990s, neuroscientists studied the brain of the rhesus monkeys and discovered a new type of neurons, known as mirror neurons, located in the area where the rhesus monkeys were operating. When one monkey observed another monkey carrying out a targeted act (e.g., taking an apple out of a box or drinking water with a glass), its mirror would discharge the neurons, as if the observer himself had done the same. In fact, looking at the monkey's brain is mirroring the action that it's seeing. Because the brain of primates is very similar to that of humans in many ways, this discovery leads scientists to make a large number of predictions about the effects of mirror neurons in humans. A famous scientist even predicted that mirror neurons meant the same thing to psychology as DNA discovery did to biology (Ramanchandran, 2000). But how much evidence do we have to support these ideas?

p103.original: 镜像神经元的发现者之一贾科莫·里佐拉蒂（Giacomo Rizzolatti）认为这些特异性神经元的放电伴随着对他人意图的理解（Rizzolatti et al.，2006）。例如，当你看见一个人在微笑时，你的镜像神经元放电了，这可能是你感受到了与微笑相联系的感觉。这些反过来促进了你与他人交流的能力，甚至促进了同理心的发展。里佐拉蒂和他的合作者甚至把这一观点往前推进了一步，提出镜像神经元的功能障碍可能是孤独症谱系障碍中社交能力受损的背后机制（Dapretto et al.，2006）。
p103.en: One of the authors of the mirror neurons, Giacomo Rizzolatti, believes that the discharge of these particular neurons is accompanied by an understanding of the intentions of others (Rizzolatti et al., 2006). For example, when you see a person smiling, your mirror neurons discharge, which may be how you feel about the smile. These, in turn, contribute to your ability to communicate with others and even to the development of common sense. Rizorati and his collaborators even took this view forward by suggesting that the functional impairment of mirror neurons may be the back-up mechanism for impairment of social capacity in autism spectrum disorders (Dapretto et al., 2006).

p104.original: 然而，批评者指出镜像神经元追捧者的某些极端观点中存在几个问题（Kilner & Lemon，2013）。一个问题是相关-因果谬误（correlation-causation fallacy）。例如，仅仅因为当我们观察到另一个人进行某项运动时我们自己的运动皮层也会被激活，我们不能得出神经元的放电使得我们能理解那个动作这一结论。它的原因可能是相反的：我们对这个行为的识别（基于我们自己过去完成这个动作的记忆）可以激发这些神经元放电（Hickok，2009）。因此，现阶段提出孤独症患者缺乏模仿能力是因为镜像神经元受损这一观点还为时尚早。如果研究人员忽视了孤独症研究中其他有前途的方向而偏好这一观点，这种做法可能就是危险的（Hickok，2014）。仅仅因为两件事情之间存在相关联系并不意味着我们可以假设其中一件事是另一件事的原因。
p104.en: Critics, however, point to several problems in some extreme views of mirror neurons (Kilner & Lemon, 2013). One problem is the relevance of the culpability-causation fallacy. For example, just because our own sports cortex is activated when we see another person carrying out a movement, we cannot draw the conclusion that the discharge of neurons makes us understand that action. The reason for this may be the opposite: our identification of this behaviour (based on our own memory of the past of doing this) can stimulate the discharge of these neurons (Hickok, 2009). It is therefore too early to raise the point that autism patients lack imitation capacity at this stage because of the loss of mirror neurons. This may be a dangerous practice if researchers ignore other promising directions in autism research (Hickok, 2014). Just because there is a correlation between two things does not mean that we can assume that one is the reason for the other.

p105.original: 第二个问题，也可能是更重要的一点是镜像神经元的活动意味着观察者理解动作的含义或意图（而不是简单的识别）的这种看法。例如，如果你看见玛丽拿起一个杯子，你可能就会从她拿杯子的方式推测出她想要喝水（而不是想要把杯子给别人）。镜像神经元追捧者认为镜像神经元这一概念包含了对动作的理解，换句话说，镜像神经元的活动促使人们对他人的动机和行为有更深的理解，并由此得出一个更普遍的结论：镜像神经元是共情和社会理解的神经基础。但是镜像神经元之外的其他领域的研究清楚地显示理解他人的动机可以不需要镜像神经系统的参与，它可以部分通过分析思维技能获得（Hickok，2010；Keysers，2010）。因此，镜像神经元是人类共情反应的根源这一假设并没有得到研究支持，并且这一假设忽略了对共情原因的其他研究发现。
p105.en: The second and perhaps more important point is that the activity of mirror neurons means that observers understand the meaning or intent of the action (rather than simple identification). For example, if you see Mary pick up a cup, you'll probably guess from the way she gets it that she wants to drink (not give it to someone else). Mirror neurons admirers believe that the concept of mirror neurons contains an understanding of actions, in other words, the activity of mirror neurons leads to a deeper understanding of the motives and behaviour of others and leads to a more general conclusion that mirror neurons are the nerve basis of mutual and social understanding. However, studies in other areas than mirror neurons clearly show that the motivation to understand others can be achieved without the involvement of the mirror nervous system, in part through analytical thinking skills (Hickok, 2010); Keysers, 2010. Therefore, the assumption that mirror neurons are the root cause of human co-habitation is not supported by research and that this hypothesis ignores other research findings on co-benefits.

p106.original: 总而言之，虽然镜像神经元回路的发现确实令人兴奋，并且它可能确实是理解人类思维、情绪和行为的一大重要进展，但是我们必须提醒自己非凡的主张需要强有力的证据，而在此之前，我们需要克制一下自己的热情。
p106.en: In sum, while the discovery of mirror neurons is indeed exciting and may indeed be a significant advance in understanding human thinking, emotions and behaviour, we must remind ourselves that extraordinary claims require strong evidence, and until then we need to contain our enthusiasm.

p108.original: 双侧额叶的后面有两大块皮层，专门负责感觉（见图2-15）。顶叶（parietal lobes）使我们可以感受热水澡的温暖、丝绸的光滑、肘击的粗暴和抚摸的温柔。躯体感觉皮层（somatosensory cortex）是顶叶上的一条特殊地带，它对临近的运动皮层带（位于额叶）进行镜像。躯体感觉皮层有两个主要功能：第一，它是全身触觉、温度觉、痛觉和应激觉的主要加工区（Graziano et al.，2000；Helmuth，2000）；第二，它将这些信息与身体的心理地图（图2-16中的小矮人）关联起来，帮助我们定位这些信息的来源。
p108.en: Two cortexes, dedicated to feeling, are behind the double frontal leaves (see figure 2-15). Parietal lobes allow us to feel warm baths, smooth silk, rough elbow punches and gentle touch. The somatic cortex is a special zone on the top of the leaves, which mirrors the adjacent cortex belt (located on the forehead). The cortex has two main functions: first, it is the main processing area for all-body touch, temperature, pain and stress (Graziano et al., 2000); Helmuth 2000; Secondly, it links this information to the psychological map of the body (the dwarfs in figures 2-16) and helps us to locate the sources of this information.

p109.original: 顶叶中的其他区域会追踪身体各个部位的位置，使你不会咬到自己的舌头或踩到自己的脚趾。当你的腿麻了的时候，除了刺痛感你不会有其他任何感觉，这是因为你暂时性地切断了神经细胞的信号，这些神经细胞本来要将感觉信息传送到顶叶的身体地图。
p109.en: Other regions of the top leaf track the location of various parts of the body so that you do not bite your tongue or step on your toes. When your legs are numb, you have no other feelings than stinging, because you temporarily cut off the signals of the neurons that were going to send the feeling to the top of the body map.

p110.original: 两个半球的顶叶各有所长。除了感觉加工和身体部位追踪之外，右顶叶还帮助我们在三维空间中定位我们感觉到的物体的位置。它为我们的日常生活提供导航，从起床到走向浴室，穿上衣服，再到上学或上班，等等。左顶叶也有自己的特殊能力。它专门从事数学推理和语音来源的定位（例如，有人叫你的名字时）。它也和颞叶合作来提取言语和文字中的意义。
p110.en: The tops of the two hemispheres are each headed. In addition to sensory processing and body tracking, the right top leaves help us locate the objects we feel in three dimensions. It provides navigation for our daily lives, from getting up to going to the bathroom, getting dressed, going to school or to work, etc. The left top leaves have their own special abilities. It specializes in mathematical reasoning and the positioning of voice sources (e.g., when someone calls your name). It also works with the leaves to extract meanings in words and words.

p111.original: 顶叶位于额叶后面，专门处理感觉。左顶叶对于数学推理很重要，右顶叶参与空间意识。
p111.en: The top leaves are behind the frontal leaves, specializing in the handling of feelings. The left top leaves are important for mathematical reasoning, and the right top leaves are involved in spatial consciousness.

p113.original: 当电话铃响或喇叭声响时，声音会到达你的颞叶（temporal lobes），它位于你耳朵的上方，在大脑半球的最边上（见图2-15）。在那里，听觉皮层可以帮助你理解声音。
p113.en: When the telephone rings or the horns sound, the sound reaches your temporal lobes, which lies above your ears and at the very end of the hemisphere (see figure 2-15). There, the hearing cortex can help you understand the sound.

p114.original: 但是，颞叶并非仅仅负责听觉。大多数人左侧听觉皮层中都有一个特殊的区域（与顶叶的下方相连），被称为威尔尼克区（Wernick's area），它帮助我们加工语言的含义。当吉尔·波特·泰勒在中风期间给同事打电话求助时，她可以听见同事说话，但是听起来像是胡言乱语。她当时想着：“哦，天哪，他听起来像是在学狗叫！”（Taylor，2009）这是因为当时她的大脑的威尔尼克区受损，抑制了她的语言理解能力。语言的表达方式（口头语言和手语）似乎并不重要：对听障人士的研究发现他们理解符号语言也是通过相同的脑区（Neville et al.，1998）。
p114.en: However, the leaf is not solely responsible for hearing. Most people have a special area in the left hearing cortex (connected to the lower side of the top leaf), known as Wernick's area, which helps us process language. When Jill Potter Taylor called her colleagues during the stroke, she could hear them, but it sounded like nonsense. She thought, "Oh, my God, he sounds like a dog barking! This is because the Wilnik area of her brain was damaged at the time, inhibiting her linguistic understanding. Language expression (oral and sign language) does not seem to be important: studies of hearing impaired persons have found that they understand the symbol language through the same brain region (Neville et al., 1998).

p115.original: 颞叶包含了加工声音的听觉皮层。颞叶也参与记忆：左颞叶损伤会破坏语言记忆，而右颞叶损伤会影响艺术和音乐的记忆。
p115.en: The leaf contains the hearing cortex that processes the sound. The leaf is also part of memory: the left leaf damage destroys the linguistic memory, while the right leaf damage affects the artistic and musical memory.

p116.original: 威尔尼克区在左颞叶，对于理解语言至关重要。
p116.en: The Wilnick region is on the left lobe, and it is essential to understand language.

p117.original: 不过，这还不是颞叶的全部功能。部分颞叶从视觉皮层中“承包”了面孔识别的工作。另一些颞叶区域与海马一起完成了长时记忆存储这项重要的任务。甚至颞叶皮层还有一块特殊的区域专门负责感知人的身体（Kanwisher，2006；Tsao，2006）。最后，右颞叶在理解语言中的情绪方面起着重要作用，这可以解释为什么吉尔同事声音中的温和语气让她感到安心（她的大脑右半球完好无损），相信他会帮助她，尽管她听不懂他的话（Taylor，2009）。
p117.en: However, it is not yet the full function of the leaf. Some of the leaves “contracted” for facial recognition from the visual cortex. Others have done this important task of storing long-term memory with sea horses. Even a special area of the cortex is dedicated to the sensory body (Kanwisher, 2006); Tsao, 2006. Finally, the right leaf plays an important role in understanding the emotions in the language, which explains why the moderate tone in the voice of her colleague Jill reassured her (her brain is intact in the right hemisphere) and trusted that he would help her, although she could not understand his words (Taylor, 2009).

p119.original: 你有没有撞到头后感到“眼冒金星”的经历？如果有，这种感觉可能是因为你的脑后侧的枕叶（occipital lobes）受到刺激（见图2-15）。正常情况下，枕叶接收来自眼睛的信息。那里的视觉皮层整合了多种感觉信息，并将它们转化为我们周围世界的可识别的连续的图像。
p119.en: Have you ever felt the experience of "seeing Venus" when you hit your head? If so, this feeling may be due to the irritation of the back of your head (occipitatal lobes) (see figure 2-15). Under normal circumstances, pillow leaves receive information from the eyes. The visual cortex there integrates multiple sensory messages and transforms them into identifiable, continuous images of the world around us.

p120.original: 为了构建外部世界的图像，脑将输入的视觉信息分开，并将它们发送到不同的皮层区域来进行颜色、运动、形状和阴影的加工。但是，枕叶并不能单独完成全部工作。正如我们在前面提到的，它们与相邻的顶叶脑区协同工作来确定物体在空间中的位置。它们也会与颞叶一起工作来生成视觉记忆（Ishai & Sagi，1995；Miyashita，1995）。我们也应该注意到先天性盲人会使用视觉皮层来帮助他们阅读盲文（Amedi et al.，2005；Barach，2003）。
p120.en: In order to construct images of the outside world, the brain separates the visual information entered and sends them to different cortical regions for processing colours, movements, shapes and shadows. However, the pillow leaves do not complete all the work alone. As we mentioned earlier, they work with adjacent contours of the brain to determine the position of objects in space. They will also work with leaf leaves to generate visual memory (Ishai & Sagi, 1995); Miyashita, 1995. We should also note the use of visual cortex by congenital blind persons to help them read Braille (Amedi et al., 2005); Barach, 2003.

p121.original: 枕叶包含了视觉皮层，负责加工视觉刺激。
p121.en: The pillow contains a visual cortex, which processes visual irritation.

p123.original: 在完成多任务的艰巨工作时，我们的脑不仅要依赖皮层的“初级加工区域”（我们前面提到的运动、感觉、视觉和听觉皮层），也要依赖皮层的“联合区域”（见图2-17）。
p123.en: In carrying out the difficult tasks of multiple tasks, our brains rely not only on the “primary processing areas” of the cortex (motion, perception, vision and hearing layers, as we have mentioned earlier), but also on the “joint areas” of the cortex (see figure 2-17).

p124.en: Figure 2-17 Cooperation in the brain region

p125.original: 注：皮层的联合区在理解和综合来自初级脑区的输入信息上起关键作用。
p125.en: Note: The cortical joint area plays a key role in understanding and synthesizing input information from primary brain regions.

p126.original: 联合皮层（association cortex）的名字来自于人们相信复杂的思想源自于观点间的相互联合这一观念。联合皮层占据整个大脑皮层的一半以上。但是，在去往联合皮层之前，来自感觉器官的原始数据必须在皮层的专门区域进行加工。
p126.en: The name of the cortex is derived from the belief that complex ideas stem from the idea of a convergence of views. The cortex accounts for more than half of the entire cortex of the brain. However, before going to the cortex, raw data from the sensory organs must be processed in the specific area of the cortex.

p127.original: 例如，初级视觉皮层加工原始视觉刺激，像单词中有哪些字母和是否有大小写之类的。然后，视觉联合皮层解释这条信息的含义，例如，感知整个单词或句子。听觉联合皮层也对来自初级听觉皮层的数据进行类似的操作。其他的初级皮层和相联系的联合皮层也是类似的关系。因此，联合皮层对原始数据进行解释，并将它置于合适的情境中，使我们能够理解和使用数据所提供的信息。通过这种方式，遍布脑叶的不同的联合皮层解释感觉、制订计划、做出决策和为行动做准备，所有这些正是我们人类所擅长的、区别于其他动物的心理力量。
p127.en: For example, the primary visual cortex processing raw visual irritation, such as which letters in words and whether or not there are case studies. The visual cortex then explains the meaning of this information, e.g., sense the whole word or sentence. Similar operations are carried out in the hearing cortex with data from the primary auditory cortex. Other primary cortex and associated cortex are similarly related. Thus, the cortex interprets the raw data and places it in the right context, enabling us to understand and use the information provided in the data. In this way, the different cortex that spans the head explain feelings, plan, make decisions and prepare for action, all of which are the psychological forces that we humans are good at, different from other animals.

p128.original: 然而，没有哪个单一脑区独立负责情绪、记忆、人格或其他复杂的心理特质，不存在任何一项主要的技能是由单一“脑中心”完成的。相反，每一项心理或行为过程都包含了许多脑网络的协同工作，每一个脑网络都是某一项特定任务的专家（Damasio，2003；LeDoux，2002）。例如，当你在做接听电话这样简单的事时，你用你的颞叶听到电话铃声，在额叶的帮助下理解它的含义，用枕叶和顶叶进行视觉定位，在额叶、顶叶和小脑的指挥下开始拿起听筒，然后再次使用额叶和颞叶回路进行电话交谈。如果没有位于脑深处的回路（边缘系统、丘脑、脑干、小脑和其他组织结构）进行沟通，那么皮层就无法完成它的工作。
p128.en: However, no single brain region is independently responsible for emotional, memory, personality or other complex psychological traits, and none of the main skills is performed by a single “brain centre”. On the contrary, each psychological or behavioural process involves the teamwork of many brain networks, each of which is an expert on a particular mission (Damasio, 2003); LeDoux, 2002. For example, when you do a simple thing like answering a phone, you hear a telephone bell with your lobe, understand its meaning with the help of the lobe, visualize it with pillows and caps, start picking up the cane under the command of the lobe, the lobe and the small brain, and then again use the lobe and the lobe for telephone conversations. The cortex cannot do its work without communication between circuits (marginal systems, cortex, brain stem, small brain and other organizational structures) located deep in the brain.

p129.original: 很明显，脑通常会设法将“所有的信息聚集在一起”，以协调一致的方式来理解和应对这个世界。神经科学家尚不清楚它是如何做到这一点的，这已经成为现代心理学最大的谜题之一。不过，近期的研究工作提供了一些线索。我们的脑一直保持活跃状态，即使当我们睡着的时候，脑也会发出协调的脑波传遍整个皮层网络。研究人员认为这些来自间隔很远的脑区的皮层以某种方式协同活动（Buzsáki，2006）。从受孕到死亡，不管我们是在工作、玩耍、走路还是睡觉，所有这些繁忙的神经网络都在彼此协调地工作，并且在多数情况下我们对此毫无觉察。
p129.en: It is clear that the brain usually tries to “get all the information together” to understand and respond to the world in a coordinated manner. It is not yet clear to neuroscientists how it has done this, which has become one of the greatest puzzles of modern psychology. However, recent studies have provided some clues. Our brains remain active, and even when we fall asleep, they send coordinated brain waves all over the cortical network. These cortexes, which come from far apart brain regions, are considered by researchers to work together in some way (Buzsáki, 2006). From conception to death, whether we are working, playing, walking or sleeping, all these busy nervous networks work in harmony with each other and, in most cases, we do not notice it.

p132.original: 分析脑两个半球的相似性和不同之处。
p132.en: Analyse the similarities and differences between the two hemispheres.

p133.original: 在我们对脑的多种结构及其功能的讨论中，我们对左右半球的功能进行了一些区分。例如，我们知道右半球受损的人不会出现言语困难，但是可能会在空间定位方面遇到一些麻烦，例如，在熟悉的地方迷路或者不能完成一副简单的拼图。这种每一个半球分管不同任务的倾向被称为大脑半球优势（cerebral dominance），这是一个经常被夸大的概念。虽然确实有些过程更多地受左半球控制，而另一些是右半球主要负责的任务，但是两个半球始终协同工作才能生成我们的思维、感受和行动。得益于胼胝体在半球间所进行的沟通工作，脑才能实现这一点。那么，左右半球有哪些不同之处呢？
p133.en: In our discussion of the multiple structures of the brain and its functions, we make some distinctions between the functions of the hemisphere and those of the hemisphere. We know, for example, that people who are damaged in the right hemisphere do not experience speech difficulties, but may experience some difficulties in spatial positioning, for example, getting lost in familiar places or failing to complete a simple puzzle. This tendency to divide tasks in each hemisphere is known as the hemispheric advantage (cerebral dominance), a often exaggerated concept. While it is true that there are processes that are more controlled by the hemisphere, while others are the primary tasks of the right hemisphere, it is the two hemispheres that work together to generate our thinking, feeling and action. This can be achieved by the brain, thanks to the inter-hemispheric communication work of the body. So what are the differences between the right and the left hemispheres?

p134.original: 胼胝体沟通左右两个半球，使左右半球可以协调我们的大多数思维、感受和行为。
p134.en: Convergence affects both hemispheres, so that they can reconcile most of our thinking, feelings and behaviours.

p136.original: 正如我们所了解的，虽然双侧脑都有一定程度的参与，但是语言功能通常是由左半球负责的。通常，左侧脑在生成和加工说话的内容上更加活跃。相比之下，右脑负责理解说话的情绪基调（Vingerhoets et al.，2003），就像我们在吉尔中风的故事中曾提到的。右脑也负责解释他人的情绪反应和他们沟通中的非言语信号。对于我们自己的情绪，负面情绪（例如，害怕和恐惧）的控制通常由右额叶负责，而左额叶通常负责调节积极情绪（例如，快乐）（Davidson，2000b）。
p136.en: As we understand it, while there is a degree of participation on both sides of the brain, language functions are usually left to the hemisphere. Usually, the left brain is more active in generating and processing the content of the speech. By contrast, the right brain is responsible for understanding the emotional tone of speech (Vingerhoets et al., 2003), as we mentioned in the story of Gil's stroke. The right brain is also responsible for explaining the emotional reactions of others and the non-verbal signals they communicate with. For our own emotions, the control of negative emotions (e.g., fear and fear) is usually the responsibility of the right leaf, while the left leaf usually regulates positive emotions (e.g., happiness) (Davidson, 2000b).

p138.original: 因此，脑的两个半球通常不会彼此竞争。相反，它们在同一个任务中起着不同的作用。用神经科学家的术语来说，两个半球有着不同却互补的加工风格。例如，左半球通过分析和语言对物体进行归类——比如，功能的相似性（小刀和勺子）；而右半球可能会根据形状和视觉模式匹配物体——比如，将硬币和闹钟配在一起，因为它们都是圆形的（Gazzaniga，1970；Sperry，1968，1982）。总之，我们可以将左半球的认知风格描述为：分析式的、线性的和序列的，而右半球则是更加整体的、情绪化的和基于空间的（Reuter-Lorenz & Miller，1998）。在功能正常的脑中，这两种风格相辅相成，生成了对世界的多重视角。
p138.en: As a result, two hemispheres of the brain do not normally compete with each other. Rather, they play a different role in the same task. In neuroscientists' terms, the two hemispheres have different but complementary processing styles. For example, the hemispheric grouping of objects through analysis and language - for example, similarity of functions (snives and spoons); The right hemisphere may match objects according to shape and visual patterns - for example, by matching coins with alarm clocks because they are round (Gazzaniga, 1970); Sperry, 1968, 1982. In short, we can describe the cognitive style of the hemisphere as analytical, linear and sequenced, while the hemisphere is more holistic, emotional and space-based (Reuter-Lorenz & Miller, 1998). In a functioning brain, the two styles complement each other and generate multiple perspectives on the world.

p139.original: 然而，一旦脑受损，就像吉尔的中风，不同的加工风格就会变得非常明显。在吉尔的故事中，她的前半生更多地依赖线性思维：“我花了37年时间热衷于以非常快的速度完成一件又一件的事情。”（Taylor，2009）她的脑左半球的损伤使她的知觉发生了根本性的转变，当她努力计划如何去求助时，她发现自己无法集中思考。这种转变立刻引起了她的注意。她曾认为理所当然的一步一步按时间进行的思维方式消失了，取而代之的是一种对自己和世界完全不同的视角。她惊叹道：“我不急于做任何事情”。她记得自己的那种快乐，感受自己与周围一切事物的联系，敏锐地捕捉他人的情绪，花时间去思考，沉浸于新视角带来的内心深处的平静。
p139.en: However, once the brain is damaged, like Jill's stroke, different processing styles become obvious. In Jill's story, her first half of her life relied more on linear thinking: “I spent 37 years trying to do one thing after another very quickly. The damage to her left hemisphere caused a fundamental change in her consciousness, and when she tried to plan how to go for help, she found herself unable to focus on it. This shift immediately drew her attention. She had taken it for granted that a step-by-step, time-based approach to thinking had disappeared and had been replaced by a completely different perspective for herself and the world. She was astonished, "I'm not in a hurry to do anything." She remembers her joy, feels her connection to everything around her, sensibly captures the emotions of others, spends her time thinking, immersed in the inner calm brought about by the new vision.

p140.original: 这听起来很像一个人在描述一种宗教的或灵性的体验，宾夕法尼亚大学的神经学研究可以告诉我们原因。研究人员对正在冥想的人进行了复杂的脑部扫描，他们发现在冥想的巅峰时期，左半球联合皮层（这个脑区使我们注意到自己身体的物理边界）的活动急剧下降。因此，冥想专家报告的自我超越和吉尔·泰勒“天人合一”的感受似乎有了生物学基础：当左半球的血流变慢时，我们关于自己是一个独立又特别的有机体的意识逐渐消失了（Newberg et al.，2001）。此外，对冥想者的研究也发现左顶叶的活动减弱与个体对身体与空间之间联系的意识有关（Newberg et al.，2001b）。
p140.en: It sounds like a person who's describing a religious or spiritual experience, and the neurology studies at the University of Pennsylvania can tell us why. Researchers have made complex brain scans of people who are meditating, and they have found a sharp decline in the activity of the hemispheric cortex, which reminds us of the physical boundaries of their bodies, at the peak of meditation. Thus, the feeling of meditation experts report that self-excessing with Jill Taylor's “one human being” seems to have a biological basis: as the blood flow slows in the hemisphere, our sense of being an independent and special organism disappears (Newberg et al., 2001). In addition, studies of meditators have found that the weakening of the left top leaves is associated with an individual's awareness of the connection between the body and space (Newberg et al., 2001b).

p141.original: 2.10.3 有些人与众不同，但这很正常
p141.en: 2.10.3 Some people are different, but it's normal.

p142.original: 让大脑半球优势变得更复杂的是，有时候，不同人的优势模式是不一样的。发现这一现象的研究采用了经颅磁刺激（transcranial magnetic stimulation，TMS）技术，该技术将强大的（但是无害的）磁脉冲穿过颅骨传送到脑。磁场会干扰脑的电活动，从而暂时性地使目标脑区失去功能。令人惊讶的是，当左侧语言区接受TMS时，有些人（通常是左撇子）的语言功能并没有受到影响。总体来说，这些研究发现大约十分之一的人主要用右脑进行语言加工。另外十分之一的人（再次强调，通常是左撇子）的语言功能由双侧脑共同承担（Knecht et al.，2002）。这表明了一个很重要的观点，尽管我们了解脑的形态，但是实际上它的精确边界在某种程度上是可变的，而且因人而异。
p142.en: What complicates the hemispheric advantage of the brain is that sometimes the patterns of advantage of different people are different. Research to detect this phenomenon has been carried out using the technology of cranscranial magnetic stimulator (TMS), which transmits powerful (but harmless) magnetic pulses through the skull to the brain. The magnetic field interferes with the electrical activity of the brain, thus temporarily rendering the target brain zone dysfunctional. Surprisingly, when TMS was accepted in the left-language area, the language function of some (usually left-handed) was not affected. In general, these studies found that about one tenth of the population uses the right brain for linguistic processing. Another tenth of the population (usually left-handed, again) has language functions shared by both brain (Knecht et al., 2002). This shows a very important point that, while we know the shape of the brain, in fact its precise boundaries are to some extent variable and vary from one person to another.

p144.original: 在一个认为“越大越好”的文化中，男性的大脑比女性的更大这一不容辩驳的事实引起了巨大的争议。当然，真正的问题是：对脑而言，尺寸真的很重要吗？大部分神经科学家认为这只是因为男性的体型更大，其实并没有什么其他的重要意义（Brannon，2008）。
p144.en: The irrefutable fact that men have larger brains than women in a culture that considers “the bigger the better” is highly controversial. Of course, the real question is: Is size really important to the brain? Most neuroscientists believe that this is only because men are larger in size, but there is no other significance (Brannon, 2008).

p145.original: 在脑中，某些结构也有性别差异。下丘脑中的某一部分被认为与性行为有关，也许还和性别认同有关。男性的这个部位比女性更大。有些研究认为男性的脑更具偏侧化，而女性倾向于将能力（例如，语言）分布在双侧脑；然而，这些领域的研究并没有得出一致的结论（Sommer et al.，2004）。如果偏侧化的差异确实存在，那么它也许可以解释为什么在中风之后女性比男性更容易恢复说话能力。除此之外，这种差异还有什么优势目前尚不清楚。
p145.en: There are also gender differences in certain structures in the brain. A part of the subdural brain is considered to be related to sexual behaviour and perhaps to gender identity. This part of the male population is larger than that of women. Some studies suggest that men's brains are more skewed, while women tend to spread their abilities (e.g. language) in both; However, research in these areas did not reach a unanimous conclusion (Summer et al., 2004). If it is true that there are slanted differences, then it may explain why women are more likely than men to recover their ability to speak after a stroke. Beyond that, it is not yet clear what the advantages of such a difference are.

p146.original: 时至今日，还没有人确定过任何一种由男性和女性的脑的生理差异所造成的心理差异。这类研究仍在继续，但是我们建议带着批判性的眼光来看待新的观点，特别要警惕那些会影响结果解释的偏见。事实上，本章的结尾部分（“批判性思维的应用”）会帮助你做到这一点。
p146.en: To date, no one has identified any psychological differences resulting from the biological differences in the brain between men and women. Such studies continue, but we suggest that new perspectives be viewed with a critical eye, especially guard against prejudices that affect the interpretation of results. Indeed, the end of this chapter (“application of critical thinking”) will help you do that.

p147.original: 2.10.5 奇怪而引人入胜的案例：裂脑人

p148.original: 想象一下，如果你的脑的两个半球不能沟通（你的脑“分裂”成两半），你的世界会变成什么样子？你会有两个“心理”吗？（见图2-18）
p148.en: Imagine what your world would be like if your two hemispheres could not communicate. Do you have two "psych"? (See figures 2-18)

p150.original: 注：当脑“分裂”成两半时，实际上只有胼胝体被切断了。这种手术会阻断两个半球沟通。令人惊讶的是，在大多数情况下，裂脑人的行为表现和正常人一样。然而，特定的实验室实验显示分裂脑会产生双重意识。
p150.en: Note: When the brain is split in half, only the gills are actually cut off. The operation would block communication between the two hemispheres. Surprisingly, in most cases, the brain-breeders behaved in the same way as normal people. However, specific laboratory experiments have shown a dual consciousness of the brain.

p151.original: 这不是一个随便聊聊的话题，因为有些人确实有“分裂的脑”。这些人往往是为了治疗持续发作的癫痫而接受了外科手术。在手术之前，这些人的脑会有不正常的放电活动，并且会在两个半球之间来回震荡，从而快速导致癫痫发作——就好像麦克风的回声突然产生很大的噪声一样。因此，医生设法切断胼胝体（连接两个半球的组织）来防止癫痫发作。但是，这需要付出心理上的代价吗？令人奇怪的是，除了极端情况外，裂脑人在心理和行为上似乎不受任何影响。
p151.en: It's not just a conversation, because some people do have a “divisive brain”. These people were often surgically operated to treat continuing epilepsy. Prior to the operation, these people's brains would have abnormal discharges and would convulsify between the two hemispheres, resulting in a rapid epilepsy — as if the echoes of the microphones suddenly had a high volume of noise. As a result, doctors have managed to cut off the epilepsy (an organization connecting the two hemispheres) to prevent epilepsy. But is that a psychological cost? Paradoxically, apart from extremes, the brain fibrosis appears to be free of any psychological or behavioural influence.

p152.original: 诺贝尔奖获得者罗杰·斯佩里（Roger Sperry）（1968）和他的同事迈克尔·加扎尼加（Michael Gazzaniga）（2005）设计非常巧妙的测试就是这些特殊情况之一。例如，如图2-19所示，裂脑人的左手握住一个球（看不见球）时，他不能通过触觉来识别这个球，但是当他用右手握住这个球时他就可以识别它。
p152.en: One of these special circumstances is the very cleverly designed test of Nobel laureate Roger Sperry (1968) and his colleague Michael Gazzaiga (2005). For example, as shown in figures 2-19, when a ball is held in the left hand of a brain-breather (who cannot see the ball), he cannot recognize it by touch, but when he holds it in his right hand, he can recognize it.

p154.original: 注：裂脑人可以准确地说出位于右手的看不见的物体是什么。但是当物体位于左手时，他不能地识别这个物体。为什么呢？
p154.en: Note: The brain-breathing person can accurately say what an invisible object is in the right hand. However, when the object was on the left hand, he could not identify it. Why?

p155.original: 我们应当如何解释这些奇怪的发现呢？让我们来看看是否能用本章的知识来解开这个奇特的难题。
p155.en: How should we explain these strange discoveries? Let's see if this chapter's knowledge can solve this strange dilemma.

p156.original: 首先，请记住胼胝体能够实现两个半球之间的通信——因此，当它被切断时，每个半球都必须自行加工信息。这也就解释了为什么裂脑人可以同时一手画圆一手画方。（对于拥有正常脑的人而言，这几乎是一个不可能完成的任务。试试吧！）
p156.en: First of all, remember that the body can achieve communication between the two hemispheres — and therefore, when it is cut off, each hemisphere must process its own information. And that explains why a man with a brain is able to draw a square with his hand. (This is almost impossible for people with a normal brain. Try it! I don't think so.

p157.original: 因为感觉通路对应着对侧皮层，每一侧身体都是与对侧脑半球通信，所以每一侧脑半球都能够感知来自对侧的手的触觉。
p157.en: Because it is felt that the path corresponds to the side cortex, each side of the body communicates with the side of the hemisphere, each side of the hemisphere is able to sense the touch of the hand from the side.

p158.original: 语言通常是左半球的功能。当这一点结合对侧感觉通路时，我们就很容易解释为什么裂脑人的左半球加工物体时可以说出物体是什么。当信息从右视野或右手（比如，右手握球）传进来时，它就被传到左半球，由于左半球的语言功能，所以裂脑人就可以说出物体是什么。相反，当物体呈现在左视野或被握在左手时，它被传到右半球进行加工，由于右半球不能说话，所以裂脑人就不能说出物体是什么。但是，他们可以通过触摸找出这个物体。
p158.en: Language is usually a function of the hemisphere. When this combines to feel the side of the road, it is easy to explain why a man with a brain fracture can say what an object is when he processes objects in the hemisphere. When the information is passed in from the right-view or right-hand (e.g., right-hand ball) it is transmitted to the left hemisphere, where, because of the language function of the left hemisphere, the brain-breathers can tell what the object is. On the contrary, when the object is presented in the left-view or held in the left hand, it is transmitted to the right hemisphere for processing and, because the right hemisphere is unable to speak, the man with the brain cannot tell what the object is. But they can find this object by touching it.

p160.original: 大脑的这种古怪表现引出了斯佩里和加扎尼加工作中最有趣的发现：裂脑人存在双重意识。当两个半球接收到不同的信息时，患者的表现就好像内心存在两个独立的个体一样。一个病人报告，他的左手经常会不合时宜地拉开裤子拉链或解开衬衫扣子，特别是当他感到压力的时候。另一个病人说，他的左手经常会不听话，会在他看电视节目的途中把电视关掉（Joseph，1988）。为什么呢？斯佩里认为右半球控制着左手，但是它几乎没有语言能力，所以它只能通过吸引注意力的某种方式来试图找到一条沟通的途径（Sperry，1964）。
p160.en: This strange manifestation of the brain leads to the most interesting finding in the work of Speri and Gaza: the bipolarity of the brain. When the two hemispheres receive different information, the patient behaves as if there were two separate individuals in his or her heart. One patient reported that his left hand was often inappropriate to pull his pants out or to unbutton his shirt, especially when he was under pressure. Another patient said that his left hand was often disobedient and that he would turn off the television on his way to watch the television programme (Joseph, 1988). Why? Speri believes that the right hemisphere controls the left hand, but it has little language skills, so it can only try to find a way to communicate in a way that attracts attention (Sperry, 1964).

p161.original: 但是，我们不能随便将裂脑人的这些发现推广到脑正常的个体中，我们必须非常谨慎。加扎尼加（1998a，1998b）建议我们将人类的心理看作是一个思想联盟（confederation of minds），它既不是单一的实体也不是双重实体，每个半球都会处理特定类型的信息。因此，对于大多数人来说，胼胝体是帮助我们的思想联盟进行信息共享的连接通道。最后，让我们再回到本节开始的核心概念2.3：脑由许多专门化的模块构成，这些模块一起工作，创造出了心理和行为（Baynes et al.，1998；Strauss，1998）。
p161.en: But we cannot simply spread these discoveries of the brain-breathers to individuals who are normal in their minds, and we must be very careful. Gaza (1998a, 1998b) recommends that we view the human mind as a coalition of ideas, neither a single entity nor a dual entity, with each hemisphere processing specific types of information. Thus, for most people, the body is a gateway to information-sharing that helps our ideological coalition. Finally, let us return to the core concept 2.3 that began in this section: the brain consists of many specialized modules that work together to create psychology and behaviour (Baynes et al., 1998); Strauss, 1998.

p163.original: 几乎每个人都认识某个因为事故、中风或肿瘤而导致脑损伤的人。你新学到的关于脑和行为的知识将会帮助你理解这些人面临的困难和问题。
p163.en: Almost everyone knows a person whose brain damage is caused by an accident, stroke or tumor. Your new knowledge of brain and behavior will help you understand the difficulties and problems faced by these people.

p164.original: 如果你知道他的哪些能力丧失了或改变了，那么你通常就可以判断出他的脑的哪些部位受损，特别是当你记住下面三条简单的原则时：
p164.en: If you know which of his abilities have been lost or changed, then you can usually judge which parts of his brain have been damaged, especially when you remember the following three simple principles:

p165.original: 1. 因为对侧加工，每一侧脑都会与对侧身体进行通信。因此，如果症状都出现在身体一侧，那么这很可能是因为对侧脑受损（见图2-20）。
p165.en: 1. Because of the side processing, each side brain communicates with the side body. Thus, if symptoms are present on both sides of the body, this is probably due to the damage to the side brain (see figure 2-20).

p166.original: 图2-20 脑半球损伤对对侧身体的影响
p166.en: Figure 2-20 Effects of hemispheric damage on side bodies

p167.original: 2. 对大部分人来说，语言通常是左脑的功能。
p167.en: 2. For most people, language is usually the function of the left brain.

p168.original: 3. 每个脑叶都有特定的功能：
p168.en: 3. Each leaf has a specific function:

p170.original: （2）颞叶负责听觉、记忆和面孔识别；
p170.en: (2) The leaf is responsible for hearing, memory and face recognition;

p171.original: （3）顶叶负责定位感觉的空间位置（包括体表）；
p171.en: (3) The top leaf is responsible for locating the spatial position of the feeling (including the chart);

p172.original: （4）额叶负责运动、言语和情绪的产生以及某些我们称之为“思维”或“智力”的高级心理功能。
p172.en: (4) The frontal leaves are responsible for sports, speech and emotion generation and for certain high-level psychological functions that we call “think” or “intellectual”.

p173.original: 以下是本书作者之一鲍勃（Bob，罗伯特的昵称）对脑知识的运用：
p173.en: The following is the application of brain knowledge to Bob, one of the authors of this book:

p174.original: 我没有注意到我爸爸走路的时候右脚脚趾轻轻地拖着地。但是晚上在家附近散步，爸爸跟不上妈妈轻快的脚步，这时候我妈妈注意到了爸爸的异样。我只是觉得他年纪大了，走路有点慢。
p174.en: I didn't notice my dad was walking with his right toe gently dragging on the floor. But at night, he walked around his home, and he couldn't keep up with his mother's light feet, and my mother noticed him. I just think he's old and he's a little slow.

p175.original: 爸爸也对他的症状漫不经心，但是妈妈坚持让他去看看医生。她预约了一个医生。医生安排了一次脑部扫描，结果显示在爸爸的脑左侧有一个很大的肿块，一个肿瘤。
p175.en: Dad was too careless about his symptoms, but Mom insisted that he go to a doctor. She has an appointment with a doctor. The doctor arranged a brain scan, which showed a large swelling on the left side of the father's brain, a tumor.

p176.original: 你可以在图2-21中看到，图2-21是穿过双耳的头部扫描图。
p176.en: As you can see in graphs 2-21, graphs 2-21 are head scans through both ears.

p178.original: 注：这是一张头部的冠状切面图，图中显示脑左侧与右脚相关的脑区有一个很大的肿块。在图的底部，我们可以看到小脑的横切面。从图中我们同样可以看到大脑皮层的褶皱。在图的中央，你可以看到两个脑室（充满脑脊液的空腔），阿尔茨海默病的病人的脑室经常会增大，这里的脑室也有点增大。这张扫描图来自本书作者之一鲍勃·约翰逊的父亲。
p178.en: Note: This is a head coronal cut-off that shows a large swelling of the brain area on the left side of the brain associated with the right foot. At the bottom of the picture, we can see the cross-section of the small brain. We can also see the wrinkles of the cortex of the brain. In the center of the chart, you can see two brain chambers, which tend to grow in the case of Alzheimer's patients, and a little in the case of the brain room. This scan is from Bob Johnson's father, one of the authors of this book.

p179.original: 基于本章中你学到的关于脑的知识，你能说出扫描图中的哪些内容可以解释病人的症状吗？
p179.en: Based on the knowledge you have learned about the brain in this chapter, can you tell what is in the scan to explain the patient's symptoms?

p180.original: 看到这幅图片的时候，我立刻就明白出了什么问题。肿瘤所在的位置会影响脑对脚的追踪定位。每一侧脑都会和对侧身体进行通信，这就很容易理解为什么出现在爸爸的脑的左侧（图的右边）的肿瘤会影响左半球与右脚之间的交流。
p180.en: When I saw this picture, I realized immediately what was wrong. The location of the tumor affects the tracking of the brain to the foot. Each side of the brain communicates with the side body, which makes it easy to understand why tumors on the left side of the father's head (the right side of the picture) affect communication between the hemisphere and the right foot.

p181.original: 神经学家还告诉我们病变组织不在脑里面。相反，它位于脑和脊髓周围的囊状层。在这份糟心的报告中，这是一个好消息。尽管如此，肿瘤正在长大并给脑造成压力。医生的建议是几周后进行手术治疗。
p181.en: Neurologists also told us that the pathological tissue is not in the brain. Instead, it is located in the cylindrical layers around the brain and spinal cord. That is good news in this terrible report. Nevertheless, the tumors are growing and exerting pressure on the brain. The doctor suggested surgery in a few weeks.

p182.original: 在这段困难时期，我为我的专业训练感到欣慰。作为一名心理学家，我对脑、脑疾病和治疗有所了解。这使我可以在儿子和心理学家之间来回切换视角。当我想到我父亲的脑正在疾病中挣扎，这种切换可以帮助我处理我自己的情绪。
p182.en: I am pleased with my professional training during this difficult period. As a psychologist, I know something about brain disease and treatment. This allows me to switch perspectives between my son and the psychologist. When I think of my father's brain struggling with disease, this switch can help me deal with my own emotions.

p183.original: 令人难过的是，手术并没有出现我们希望的奇迹。虽然每年都有成千上万的人接受了脑部手术，很多人的生活质量得到了提升，寿命延长了，但是要记得这是在给重症患者进行手术。事实上，手术确实让爸爸有了更多的时间可以陪伴我们。
p183.en: Sadly, the surgery did not produce the miracle we wanted. Although thousands of people undergo brain surgery every year, many have improved their quality of life and have increased their longevity, it is important to remember that this is an operation for people with severe illnesses. In fact, the operation did give Dad more time to be with us.

p184.original: 心理学很有用 接触式运动和创伤性脑损伤
p184.en: Psychology works. Contact motion and traumatic brain damage.

p185.original: 尽管我们的脑具有惊人的能力和可塑性，可以从受伤和疾病中完全或部分康复，但是我们的脑仍然是一个脆弱的器官。它并不总是能够从创伤中恢复过来。近年来，随着接触式运动造成的创伤性脑损伤（traumatic brain injury，TBI）的例子越来越多，公众对脑需要保护的认识也日益增强。
p185.en: Despite the amazing ability and plasticity of our brains to recover completely or partially from injuries and diseases, our brains remain a fragile organ. It does not always recover from trauma. In recent years, as more examples of traumatic brain damage (traumatic brain injury, TBI) resulting from contact movements have become available, there has also been a growing public awareness of the need for brain protection.
