p186.original: 一个知名的案例是2012年传奇橄榄球巨星朱尼·西沃（Junior Seau）的自杀悲剧。西沃的故事很励志，他是一位坚强又勇猛的球员、一个聪明的商人和一个深受人们爱戴的圣迭戈市民，他致力于帮助高危青年，多年来他付出了沉重的代价来为大家敲响警钟：他的尸检报告显示他患有与脑震荡史有关的慢性脑部疾病。他的前队友纳特罗内·米恩斯（Natrone Means）说：“我们是‘闻一下嗅盐，醒过来就回到场上去’的一代。”尽管他性格开朗，但是认识他的人都认为，在他的最后几年里，朱尼已经不再是他自己了。他的行为变得越发古怪，失眠困扰着他，并且他做了一系列越来越糟糕的决定。最终，他结束了自己的生命。
p186.en: A well-known case was the suicide tragedy of Junior Seau, a legendary football star in 2012. The story of Sevo is heartening, a strong and courageous player, a smart businessman and a beloved citizen of San Diego, committed to helping youth at risk, who has spent a heavy price ringing alarms for years: his autopsy report shows that he suffers from chronic brain diseases associated with the history of concussion. His ex-team mate, Natrone Means, said, “We are the generation of ‘smelting salt and waking up and going back to the field’. “Despite his openness, all those who knew him believed that Juni had ceased to be himself in his last years. His behaviour has become more eccentric, insomnia has plagued him and he has made a series of increasingly bad decisions. Eventually, he ended his life.

p187.original: 令人难过的是，西沃的故事并非单一个案。最近的一项研究查看了美国职业橄榄球联盟运动员的医疗记录，发现大约有30%的人曾经历过认知障碍——这个比例明显高于普通人（O’Brien，2014）。不仅仅是橄榄球，从足球到滑雪等运动引起的脑震荡都会造成创伤性脑损伤，而拳击和综合格斗尤为严重。也许最令人不安的是，它也会影响参加接触式运动的儿童和青少年：急诊室每年都要治疗25万名参加运动受了脑外伤的年轻人（White House Fact Sheet，2014）。根据美国疾病控制与预防中心的数据，年轻运动员反复脑震荡会导致永久性的脑损伤（CDC's Heads Up Program，Concussion Fact Sheet，2013）。
p187.en: Sadly, the story of Sevo is not a single case. A recent study, which examined the medical records of professional football league players in the United States, found that about 30 per cent of the population had experienced cognitive disorders — a significantly higher percentage than the average population (O'Brien, 2014). Not just football, brain concussions caused by sports ranging from football to ski can cause traumatic brain damage, especially in the case of boxing and combined combat. Perhaps most disturbingly, it will also affect children and adolescents involved in the contact movement: an emergency room will treat 250,000 young people who have suffered brain trauma every year from the movement (white House Fact Sheet, 2014). According to data from the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, repeated concussions among young athletes lead to permanent brain damage (CDC's Heads Up Programme, Concussion Fact Sheet, 2013).

p188.original: 在布防期间和布防之后，战斗人员也经常会出现创伤性脑损伤。简易爆炸装置的爆炸也会引起脑震荡或TBI。由于TBI是内伤，所以经常被忽略，退伍军人回家之后却因失眠、头疼、头晕、平衡和注意力问题而苦苦挣扎。然而，这些TBI的典型症状是可以被治愈的，只要它们被诊断出来。
p188.en: During and after emplacement, combatants also often experience traumatic brain damage. Improvised explosive devices also cause concussions or TBI. Since TBI is an internal injury, it is often ignored and veterans come home and struggle with insomnia, headaches, dizziness, balance and attention problems. However, these typical TBI symptoms can be cured as long as they are diagnosed.

p189.original: 美国职业橄榄球联盟的超级巨星西沃的自杀悲剧引起了人们对接触式运动造成的创伤性脑损伤的关注。
p189.en: The suicide tragedy of the superstar Syvo of the Professional Football League of the United States raised concerns about traumatic brain damage caused by contact movements.

p190.original: 幸运的是，专业机构和青年组织开始认真对待TBI，对脑震荡进行更常规的筛查，努力开发保护性更好的头盔，并对脑震荡给予更严格和更早的治疗。在军队中，大量资源被投入脑损伤的检测和治疗中，以期实现更早和更有效的检测与治疗。这对我们所有人来说都是一个好消息：虽然TBI因受伤的士兵和运动员的故事而获得关注，但有更多的人因跌倒或车祸等常见情况而使脑部受伤。加利福尼亚大学神经外科医生格里·曼利（Gerry Manley）指出，许多有TBI的人从来没有接受过诊断，因此他们终其一生从感觉到说话，从语言再到认知加工，甚至情绪修复等方面存在长期问题。事实上，每50个美国人中就有一个存在TBI引起的残疾，每年会花费770亿美元的国家医疗保健费用（Norris，2013）。如果你希望获取更多信息，请读者查看脑创伤基金会（Brain Trauma Foundation）的网站和美国疾病控制与预防中心的HEADS UP计划。
p190.en: Fortunately, professional institutions and youth organizations have begun to take TBI seriously, conducting more routine screening of concussions, working to develop more protective helmets and providing stricter and earlier treatment for concussions. In the military, significant resources are invested in the detection and treatment of brain damage with a view to achieving earlier and more effective testing and treatment. This is good news for all of us: while TBI has received attention for the stories of wounded soldiers and athletes, more people have suffered brain injuries as a result of common circumstances, such as falling or car crashes. Gerry Manley, a neurosurgeon at the University of California, stated that many people with TBI had never been diagnosed, so they had long-term problems with their lives, from feeling to talking, from language to cognitive processing, and even emotional healing. Indeed, one in every 50 Americans has a TBI-induced disability, which costs $77 billion a year for national health care (Norris, 2013). If you want more information, you can see the website of the Brain Trauma Foundation and the HEADS UP programme of the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

p193.original: 通过他从事的运动或工作和爱好，确定你认识的某个人可能会有TBI的风险。使用你学到的知识，写一个简短的说明让他了解TBI的症状，你可以用便条或者对话的形式。
p193.en: Through his sport or work and hobbies, make sure someone you know may be at risk from TBI. Using the knowledge you have learned, write a short note to make him aware of the symptoms of TBI, you can use it in the form of notes or conversations.

p194.original: 批判性思维的应用：左脑与右脑
p194.en: Application of critical thinking: left and right

p195.original: 大部分人真具有左脑优势或右脑优势吗？还是真相其实没有那么简单？
p195.en: Do most people really have a left or right brain advantage? Or is the truth not that simple?

p196.original: 你更愿意解一道数学题还是创作一幅画？写一篇学术文章还是编一个故事？根据流行科学的说法，你对这类问题的回答揭示了你是一个“左脑人”还是一个“右脑人”。并且，他们还会鼓励你根据这个信息进行职业选择。这些说法科学吗？
p196.en: Would you rather solve a math problem or create a painting? An academic article or a story? According to popular science, your answer to such questions reveals whether you are a “left brain man” or a “right brain man”. And they'll encourage you to make career choices based on this information. Is that a science?

p197.original: 裂脑人研究和脑双侧加工信息的差异已经引起了公众的兴趣。媒体声称左脑是逻辑脑，右脑是情绪脑。这很容易使人得出错误的结论：你的朋友贾马尔偏好分析，他的生活主要依靠左脑；而贾马尔的妻子巴布对别人的情绪更加敏感，她主要依靠右脑来处理生活经历。
p197.en: Differences in the research and processing of information on both sides of the brain have generated public interest. The media claim that the left brain is the logical brain and the right brain is the emotional brain. This can easily lead people to the wrong conclusion: your friend Jamal's preference analysis, whose life depends mainly on the left brain; Jamal's wife, Babu, is more sensitive to the emotions of others and relies mainly on her right brain to deal with life experiences.

p198.original: 伪科学家对此一见钟情，知道这一定会成为一种时尚，他们开设了很多工作坊来帮助那些分析型的人开发他们的“右脑”。在你加入这个特殊潮流之前，让我们深入了解一下这个问题。人们完全属于这一类或那一类这种想法很符合大众的口味，但是事实果真如此吗？神经科学的近期发现能够告诉我们左右脑是如何互动的，以及人们是否具有左脑优势或右脑优势。那么，为了获得这个流行观念的真相，我们需要提出和回答哪些问题？
p198.en: The pseudo-scientists love this at first sight, knowing that it must be a fashion, and they have set up workshops to help those who are analysts develop their “right brain”. Before you join this special trend, let us get a little deeper into this. It is in the public taste of people who belong entirely to this category or categories, but is it true that this is true? Recent discoveries in neuroscience can tell us how the right and right brain interact, and whether people have a left or right brain advantage. So, what questions do we need to ask and answer in order to get the truth about this prevailing concept?

p199.original: 这个观点是合理的还是极端的？
p199.en: Is that a reasonable or extreme point of view?

p200.original: 正如我们本章所了解的，我们依赖单侧脑，而几乎不用另一侧脑的这种说法是一种夸大之词。相反，我们同时使用双侧脑，它们彼此协作。正如我们经常在极端观点中看到的，“左脑还是右脑”的议题过度简化了左右脑差异的科学发现：人们很少能被完全归为二分法中的一类。这个例子很好地说明了诚实的科学发现（例如，本章节提到的左右半球差异的工作）进入流行新闻媒体后往往会被盲目夸大。我们应该始终以合理的、怀疑的态度来理解这些报道，并仔细查看它们的证据。
p200.en: As we know in this chapter, it is an exaggeration to rely on one side of the brain, and almost without the other. Instead, we use both sides of the brain, and they work together. As we often see in extreme views, the topic of “left brain or right brain” oversimplifies scientific findings of the right and right brain differences: people are rarely classified as a complete dichotomy. This example is a good example of how honest scientific findings (e.g., the work of the right and right hemispheric differences mentioned in this chapter) tend to be exaggerated blindly when they enter the popular news media. We should always understand these reports with reasonable and skepticism and look closely at their evidence.

p202.original: 正如我们所了解的，两个脑半球的工作风格有所不同，但是两个工作半球的实际差异并没有比它们的相似之处多很多（Banich，1998；Trope et al.，1992）。最重要的，也是那些左右脑追捧者所忽略的，是完整的脑的两个半球始终彼此合作，互为补充，为我们的心理生活做出贡献。
p202.en: As we know, the working styles of the two hemispheres differ, but the actual differences between the two hemispheres are not much more similar than they are (Banich, 1998); Trans et al., 1992. What is most important, which is ignored by those who are right or wrong, is that the two hemispheres of the whole brain always work together to complement each other and contribute to our psychological lives.

p203.original: 相关结论是否存在被偏差污染的可能？
p203.en: Is there a risk of contamination by deviation?

p204.original: 当我们考虑这个问题时，很容易想到两种偏差。第一个是我们曾提到过的，某些企业通过“贩卖”这种观点赚到了钱，如果这家企业试图让你相信这个观点是真实可靠的，那么这肯定会产生一种明显的偏差。还可能出现情感偏差（emotional bias）。毕竟我们人类喜欢把人和事物归类：它迎合了我们对秩序感的需要，并带给我们解决了复杂问题的满足感。不足为奇的是，我们经常使用类型学来解释人性、特征和行为，具体做法就是把它们归入过度简化的类别中。
p204.en: When we think about it, it is easy to think of two deviations. The first is the fact that some businesses have made money through the idea of “trafficking”, as we have mentioned, and if the enterprise tries to convince you that this view is true, it will certainly create a clear deviation. There may also be emotional deviations. After all, we human beings like to classify people and things: it meets our needs for a sense of order and gives us a sense of satisfaction in solving complex problems. Not surprisingly, we often use typologies to explain humanity, characteristics and behaviour, by classifying them in an overly simplified category.

p205.original: 我们能够得出什么结论？

p206.original: 除非你有一个分裂脑，否则你左右两侧的脑的能力都会影响你做的任何事情。那么，为什么人们在进行相同任务时有着明显的差异呢？一些人似乎以更加经过分析的、更具逻辑的方式来做事情；另一些人则会采用更直觉的、更情绪化的方式。现在你已经对脑的工作方式有所了解，你明白我们不能简单地用人们使用左脑或右脑来解释这些差异。甚至裂脑人也在使用双侧脑。对此更好的解释是个体经历和脑的生理基础之间的不同搭配。人们之所以存在差异是因为先天和后天的不同组合，而不是因为他们使用了不同的半球。
p206.en: Unless you have a split brain, the ability of both sides of your brain will affect anything you do. Why, then, is there a clear difference in the way people do the same tasks? Some seem to do things in a more analytical and logical way; Others are more intuitive and emotional. Now that you know how the brain works, you know that we can't simply explain these differences with people using the left or the right. Even the brain-breathing people are using both sides of the brain. A better explanation for this is the different mix of individual experiences and the biological basis of the brain. The difference is due to the different combinations of birth and day, not because they use different hemispheres.

p209.original: 想想你喜欢做的事情：参加某项运动或者演奏音乐，烹饪或和朋友一起吃饭，学习或购物。现在想象一下花几小时来做这件事，以及在此期间发生的每一个细节。请记下其中的某些事情，并尝试确认这项活动的哪些部分是由你的左脑主导的，哪些部分是由右脑调节的。
p209.en: Think of what you like to do: to take part in a sport or play music, cook or eat with friends, study or shop. Now imagine how many hours it takes to do this, and every detail that happens during that period. Write down some of these things and try to determine which parts of this activity are dominated by your left brain and which are regulated by your right brain.
